# Soil and particles implementation evidence

## Goal

Implement the full `SOIL_AND_PARTICLES.md` objective. The goal is active and incomplete. Implemented increments include MPM/DEM terrain-export optimization, exclusive production backend selection, retained DEM stepping with a frame-only viewer mirror, dirty material-map caching, the MPM terrain-only CPU bridge with compact GPU statistics, and opt-in compact MPM grid storage. These components do not redefine full completion.

## Fitted ADMM response storage — 2026-10-15

The actual trace exposed a component-fixture gap: active contacts grow from 251
to 283, so only 43/102 substeps fit the preceding 256-contact cache. A test-only
preallocated trace copies counts and success fields in existing submissions,
then reads once after all frames. The trace preserves all 44 state artifacts and
hot counters; its offline jq slurp/input error was corrected without a GPU rerun.

Shared core/pivot/rate arrays now fit the admitted DOF width while preserving the
32-entry core row stride and arithmetic. Aligned capacity accounting admits 298
contacts at 10 DOFs (38320 shared bytes), 84 at 32 DOFs and 512 at 1 DOF, without
raising the 38400-byte device requirement. Overflow remains defined. All 29 CPU
ADMM checks pass, and the focused GPU batch passes in 37.24 s under 90 s. Two
captured packets and 15 nonzero-response boundary/poison cases preserve exact
outputs and independent numerical/physical/rejection gates. Unselected prototype
timing arms were omitted explicitly, not marked as tested.

The identical executable passes articulated rollback (3.64 s) and four native50k
ABBA runs (68.84 s under 180 s). All 176 state artifacts are exact; all hot counters
match baseline with zero allocations. Both candidate runs have 102/102 cache hits
and the identical active-count sequence. Warm solve means are 500.965/512.294 ms
versus controls 544.090/551.983 ms (ratios 0.920740/0.928098). Warm soil means are
949.882/978.531 ms versus 1070.454/1004.743 ms. These are contended, instrumented,
three-frame observations, not clean causal or full real-time acceptance. The 4 ms
target and remaining full-plan scope remain open. Evidence:
`benchmarks/soil/2026-10-15-admm-fitted-native/SUMMARY.md`.

## Initial ADMM resident response runtime — 2026-10-15

The preceding experimental ADMM constructor selected compact resident response
coordinates with cooperative mutable-point staging, preserving ordered arithmetic
and guarded publication. The full active set must fit; overflow uses packed tiled
staging. Ten DOFs admit 256 contacts within 36256 aligned workgroup bytes. All
32 widths retain existing device admission. Standalone/default Newton is unchanged.

The preceding shared mutable-state and direct-global-point response experiments
passed correctness checks but did not establish a speedup, and remain unselected.
The final component retains exact five-buffer outputs, six boundary/poison cases
and independent failure/numerical/physical checks. Its 28 CPU checks and GPU batch
pass (52.52 s under 90 s). Component solve upper medians improve from 5.657600 to
4.938752 ms and 9.688064 to 8.865792 ms; contention limits attribution.

Runtime source equivalence to that candidate is frozen. Articulated feedback and
rollback pass (4.61 s); four native 50k actual tractor runs pass in 70.28 s under
the 180-second cap. All 176 state artifacts match the sealed original runtime
exactly, with zero hot allocations across 12 frames. Two paired warm soil ratios
are 0.970786 and 1.045121; solve ratios 0.993271 and 1.040442. No reliable integrated
speedup is established. Candidate soil means remain 1152.911 / 1199.696 ms under
100% GPU contention, far above 4 ms per simulated frame. Full-plan acceptance
and physical calibration remain open. Evidence:
`benchmarks/soil/2026-10-15-admm-response-native/SUMMARY.md`.

## ADMM publication summation — 2026-10-15

Guarded active ADMM publication now uses canonical-zero magnitude-sorted FastTwoSum:
three atomic rounding round trips per compensated sum instead of six. The source
reversal contract proves only rate_sum changes; all independent physical/numerical
and failure checks remain. Ordinary standalone/default Newton publication is unchanged.

Forty-two CPU checks and both captured packets pass in 27.63 s. Each packet also
compares 99344 finite GPU arithmetic cases exactly, covering signed zeros,
subnormals, cancellation, extremes and deterministic random pairs. All five
resident result buffers remain exact and prior failure/analytic fixtures pass.

Articulated rollback passes in 3.50 s. Four actual native 50k AB/BA processes pass
in 60.32 s, with all 176 full soil/public/internal-machine artifacts byte-exact
against the prior cooperative baseline and zero observed allocations in all frames.

Performance remains inconclusive under pre-existing 100% GPU utilization. Component
paired upper-median changes are +314.209% and -22.290%. Actual publication ratios
are 0.986/0.375, while total-soil ratios are 1.017/0.446; unchanged solve/machine
times also fall sharply in the second block. Candidate soil means of
660.704/662.755 ms do not establish 4 ms, clean causal speedup or full acceptance.
[Component controls and raw cases](benchmarks/soil/2026-10-15-admm-sorted-publication/SUMMARY.md);
[actual-workload timing and exact-state audit](benchmarks/soil/2026-10-15-admm-sorted-native/SUMMARY.md).

Resident ADMM changes only the staged-response array capacity, from 2048 vec4s
to 64 * max(DOFs, 4). Both staging arrays therefore occupy 11264 rather than
33792 bytes for the 10-DOF tractor. Arithmetic, fixed 64 iterations, global
buffers, device admission and publication checks are unchanged. Source-hashed

All 32 widths validate and 23 CPU tests pass. One frozen 36.13 s GPU batch passes
both captured packets, with all five result buffers exact against full-capacity
control on nine runs per mode. Existing lifecycle, numerical rejection, analytic
wall and geometry checks also pass. The unchanged 90-second cap includes setup.

The paired total-time upper-median changes are +3.099% and +1.202%; pre-run GPU
utilization was 100%, and samples contain large contention swings. This proves a
smaller workgroup allocation, **not a speedup, frame budget or full-plan acceptance**.
[Raw evidence and scope](benchmarks/soil/2026-10-15-admm-width-staging/SUMMARY.md).

Actual-50k native integration then passes in 15.19 s including setup. All 44
stored binaries match the pre-change native run exactly: full soil checkpoints,
public states and nine internal machine buffers at frames 0 through 3. Observed
soil times are 2034.921 / 2016.901 / 2137.791 ms under contention; no full-frame
speedup or real-time acceptance is established. A preceding harness-only
AlreadyExists failure occurred before GPU setup and is preserved separately.
[Integration and exact comparisons](benchmarks/soil/2026-10-15-admm-width-native/SUMMARY.md).

## Actual 50k ADMM tractor execution — 2026-10-15

Added a bounded actual-workload harness for both explicit ADMM constructors:
native prediction and paired Featherstone. Each runs three frames with 50000
particles, default seed/material/geometry, fixed-order P2G, 300 N m drive torque
per wheel, dt=1/60, max substep 0.0005, 34 substeps, 4096 contact slots and 64
ADMM iterations. Existing Newton defaults are unchanged. CPU workload contract,
both execution tests and CPU artifact comparison pass in the frozen follow-up.
The combined GPU/compare batch takes 92.65 s under the unchanged 180 s cap.

Initial conditions match exactly. Across three frames, maximum native versus
Featherstone differences are 1.192092896e-7 for particle positions,
3.874301910e-7 for particle velocities and 7.660009018e-7 for six-body poses and
velocities, all below the unchanged 2e-5 bound. Full soil checkpoints and nine
machine buffers are also saved, but complete internal-state equivalence, forces,
joint-rate parity and longer trajectories are not established by this comparison.

Each successful step observes zero GPU buffer allocations, 884 bytes of completion
readback, 19796 upload bytes on frame one and 18964 thereafter. Native dispatches
are 1803/frame; paired Featherstone dispatches are 1769/frame. Profile/load/raw-state
readbacks occur outside the timed step and resource scopes. Detailed profiling
captures 102 contact and 272 preparation intervals per frame, with no falsely
labelled Newton work records. Summed top-level soil stages exclude double-counting
their nested contact/preparation scopes.

| Prediction | Soil GPU ms, frames 2 / 3 | Step wall ms, frames 2 / 3 | Setup ms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Paired Featherstone | 968.552 / 1031.901 | 2171.196 / 2179.438 | 71879.167 |
| Native | 1850.066 / 1887.160 | 3607.210 / 3662.146 | 1750.806 |

These measurements fail 4 ms and 60 FPS. They are not an uncontended comparison:
the RTX 4080 was already at 100% utilization before the run, with Astrocraft using
5596 MiB plus display/remote-desktop workloads. Telemetry is retained; none were
stopped. Detailed instrumentation, arm order and just two post-cold samples also
preclude percentile or intrinsic solver-speed conclusions. Contact preparation,
solve and publication dominate observed soil intervals; non-contact soil work
is approximately 22 ms/frame in the native records and is not negligible either.

The first 70.38 s batch failed before stepping because the new harness requested
a public committed checkpoint at frame zero. Both constructors completed, but
the lifecycle guard correctly rejected the read. That failed batch is sealed.
Initial raw capture now explicitly checks public rejection and uses the test-only
simulation reference; production commitment/publication logic was not weakened.

Actual short-run execution/parity is established; performance optimization,
long-horizon/internal-state comparisons, rendered agricultural behavior and physical
calibration remain open. Evidence:
`benchmarks/soil/2026-10-15-admm-tractor-initial-state/SUMMARY.md`.

## Articulated-world ADMM, profiling and exact rollback — 2026-10-15

Added a distinct ADMM retained projection mode with paired-rate admission,
grid-aware budgets, friction configuration queries, explicit backend reporting
and ADMM-labelled eight-word fault diagnostics. Shared preparation failure capture
uses ADMM-specific paths; Newton solver/history schemas are not assigned to ADMM.
Added tractor constructors for paired Featherstone and native prediction with
explicit grid/transfer choices. Existing Newton constructors and defaults remain.

The native-prediction all-contact fixture uses six-body tractor geometry, 65 soil
particles, five loaded wheel/tine bindings and three substeps per frame. Four
measured frames pass existing linear/angular impulse and combined momentum gates,
including affine and elastic soil energy. Maximum angular error is 5.541868985e-9,
linear impulse error 1.089865101e-8 and combined momentum error 7.050566069e-8.
Thresholds remain 2e-5, 2e-5 and 2e-4 respectively; the underlying ADMM numerical
publication remains 1e-6. Control-edit rollback/retry and injected GPU-status fault
rollback/retry pass; soil and nine machine/compensation buffers restore exactly,
and the rebuilt ADMM owner commits frame six. This is zero-gravity integration
evidence, not an agricultural calibration, actual 50k field run or rendered proof.

The first frozen batch failed in 2.23 s at detailed timestamp readback after the
first physical frame. ADMM now emits traced preparation phases through the shared
strict eight-stage profile contract, including an empty optional-history scope
as Newton already does with history disabled. No validator or query-budget gate
was weakened. The next 5.06 s batch passed four physical/profile frames but failed
exact rollback: one scalar joint_qd word differed while paired rates and the other
eight machine buffers matched. RuntimeRates now borrows both scalar mirrors and
restores their high words from paired checkpoints with failure-only GPU copies.
This adds no retained allocation, host conversion or normal-step dispatch.

Twenty-eight CPU checks pass. The following batch passed direct rate lifecycle
(0.71 s) and articulated world integration (4.55 s), then failed a stale literal
in the grid-budget test; the entire 6.13 s batch remains recorded as failed.
Independent current arithmetic already matched all modes. Corrected literals are
36420 sticking bytes and 362268 unilateral bytes at the existing compact fixture.
Only that changed budget test was rerun: 1.91 s, all seven modes, dense identity,
active storage, compact world sizes 17/96/1536, invalid dimensions and tile growth
pass. ADMM's 125-tile/128-slot/3-DOF budget is 410296 bytes. All source hashes except
the two-assertion budget test match the sealed passing world/lifecycle run.

Fault injection validates rollback and labels, not a complete ADMM solver replay
schema. Repeated preparation capture paths report existing-file errors rather
than overwrite earlier immutable captures. Actual 50k constructor execution,
native/Featherstone trajectory parity, long horizons and 4 ms/60 FPS remain open.
Evidence: `benchmarks/soil/2026-10-15-admm-world-budget-fix/SUMMARY.md`.

## Guarded ADMM in prepared MPM coupling — 2026-10-15

Added explicit experimental ADMM selection in `PreparedMpmUnilateralCoupling`,
with grid-aware budget queries and public paired machine publication. Internal
method selection distinguishes projection, Newton and ADMM rather than reusing
the Newton boolean. ADMM has no Newton history or Newton solver-failure packet;
its preparation packet is exposed separately. Existing candidate certification,
particle-fault bridge, reaction wrenches and status-gated grid/particle publication
are used without bypasses. Private encode phases preserve dispatch order while
providing honest coarse preparation, solve and publication profile scopes.

Twenty-two focused CPU checks pass. A frozen 23.91 s RTX 4080 batch passes both
the new integration test (8.14 s) and existing captured replay/geometry checks
(15.75 s). The integration fixture uses 65 particles, 3 machine DOFs, 128 candidate
slots and four successful steps per configuration. Dense, active, compact and
profiled-dense runs match all 13 final checkpoint/rate/status/wrench buffers exactly.
Maximum normalized machine impulse/momentum error is 9.260006817e-9 against 1e-6;
paired rate-delta agreement retains the 2e-14 bound. Profiling records three
contact stages per substep, bounded by the parent projection interval, without
changing the solution. Stepping observes no allocation/readback; normal MPM input
uploads remain. Dense coupling owned-byte admission is 171320 bytes for this case.

A one-slot candidate overflow rejects without advancing particles. Negative mass
produces preparation fault 2, zero rate/world/reaction outputs and unchanged nine
particle checkpoint buffers. Machine publication sets fault 32 without mutating
rates/deltas. Repaired inputs remain rejected until explicit reset; recovery
passes. Injected latched particle-grid metadata faults propagate to common status
and block machine publication in all four configurations. This is a bridge fault
injection, not a new physical invalid-particle trajectory test. Budget-minus-one
rejection occurs before any observed allocation. Existing captured exactness,
numerical guards and archived failing comparisons remain unchanged.

Articulated tractor-world integration, full-frame rollback/trajectories, dense
contacts, calibration and 50k/4 ms acceptance remain open. Batch duration is not
a speed comparison. Frozen source/harness/executable/input and outputs:
`benchmarks/soil/2026-10-15-admm-mpm-integration/SUMMARY.md`.

## Analytic geometry-to-ADMM adapter — 2026-10-15

Added the public experimental `ExperimentalSoilAdmmGeometryGpu` adapter. Analytic
geometry feeds checked GPU preparation, mandatory guarded ADMM publication and
the existing world-space recovery shader. The original Newton bridge program
is shared, with no shader or default-backend changes. Capacity, input usage/size,
device limits and owned-byte budget are checked before allocation. The adapter
owns 27 observed buffers; 3-DOF capacities of 0/1, 65 and 4096 slots require
1124, 42084 and 2621924 bytes respectively.

Twenty CPU checks and one frozen 17.80 s RTX 4080 batch pass. Six fixtures run
per captured packet: empty sphere, frictionless sphere, frictional box, sphere
with an X wall, cylinder with X/Z walls and a sparse frictional sphere layout.
There are at most two active contacts, at distinct surface points, even in the
65/4096-slot layouts. Across 12 fixture executions, maximum independent physical
error is 8.940696716e-8, projected residual 2.235174179e-8 and CPU-reference delta
4.180212332e-8. Paired rates, analytic normals/gaps, world velocities/impulses,
wall signs, inactive zeros, exact repeats and reset recovery are checked.

Negative friction and invalid mass fail closed; repaired inputs do not clear a
latched fault without reset. Common status exposes preparation, solver and
publication faults separately; geometry diagnostics are consumable only when
common status is zero. Nonempty encode has eight dispatches, empty encode six,
with zero observed allocation/upload/readback. Budget rejection allocates nothing.
Existing captured exactness, numerical guards and retained failures still pass
their unchanged audit. Runtime batch duration is not solver performance evidence.

MPM/tractor selection, dense contacts, long trajectories, calibration and full-frame
4 ms/60 FPS acceptance remain open. Evidence:
`benchmarks/soil/2026-10-15-admm-geometry-adapter/SUMMARY.md`.

## Resident guarded ADMM API — 2026-10-15

Added the public experimental `soil_admm_gpu` module, exposing prepared input
bindings, bounded capacity, byte-budget admission, persistent buffers and explicit
reset/encode. Certified output/rate/status buffers are public; test-only internal
diagnostics and publication bypass hooks are absent from non-test builds. The API
always enables active-list validation plus physical/numerical publication and
uses uncached ordered solver mode3. Simulator backend defaults are unchanged.

Admission supports1–32DOFs,0–16384slots and1–64iterations, requires38400bytes of
workgroup storage and the existing prepared SPD/response contract. Required owned
bytes are304*max(slots,1)+4*(max(slots,1)+1)+8*dofs+96. The4096slot/10DOF cases
own1261748bytes over10buffers; empty1DOF owns416bytes. Encode has no observed
allocation/upload/readback and two dispatches. This is not a whole-frame residency
or50k-capacity claim.

The first frozen run failed at7.34s on an empty active-index buffer bound with4
bytes where WGSL required8. The failure remains sealed in
`2026-10-15-admm-resident-api`. Allocation, budget accounting and publisher admission
now share the corrected minimum, with Naga runtime-array layout coverage and
preallocation rejection tests. Cold-start report padding is also explicitly reset.

Fifteen CPU contracts and one frozen13.88s GPU follow-up pass: both captured
packets retain exact five-buffer replay parity, repeat/no-reset behavior, poison
recovery, upstream/NaN contact fail-closed/reset, mandatory numerical rejection,
one-iteration rejection and independent-instance isolation. Empty contacts preserve
paired free rates exactly, publish zeros and repeat exactly. Prior numerical,
cache/index and archived-failure observations remain unchanged. This usable API
is still experimental: wall regimes, long trajectories, tractor integration,
full50k and4ms/60FPS acceptance remain open. Evidence:
`benchmarks/soil/2026-10-15-admm-resident-empty-fix/SUMMARY.md`.

## Independent numerical ADMM publication — 2026-10-15

Standalone experimental publication now applies the existing resident projected
contact and signed-wall residual guard at absolute1e-6. The guard was extracted
into a shared WGSL fragment, verified byte-identical to the archived resident
literal; standalone assembly changes only uniform/fault symbol names. Physical
certification, contact ownership, energy order and final failure clearing remain.

Thirteen CPU contracts pass. Initial GPU verification stopped after1.51s because
an auxiliary check assumed old resident publication status would match standalone
publication byte-for-byte. Rates and output buffers match exactly, but diagnostic
scale differs by3ULPs. That failure is sealed under
`2026-10-15-admm-publication-numerical`; it is not relabelled as passing. Follow-up
records `old_physical_only_exact:false`, checks exact fault fields/rates/outputs
and same-pipeline old-state self-repeat, then exercises the actual guard contract.

The frozen follow-up completes in2.21s. Both captured old early-stopped states are
accepted without numerical guard and rejected with fault8 when enabled, with all
rates/outputs zero. The fault persists without reset and valid ADMM output/status
recover exactly after reset. One-iteration ADMM solves report no internal solver
fault but have independent residuals1.314445556/1.312003892; publication rejects
both with fault8 and recovers exactly after restoring certified states. Valid
64-iteration ADMM retains exact prior-control/mode/nine-repeat parity and all
prior cache/index fault checks. Physical/numerical1e-6 and public2e-5 gates remain
unchanged, including the failed old-public comparison. Timings are diagnostic,
not a performance acceptance retry; no cache promotion or4ms/60FPS claim.
Evidence: `benchmarks/soil/2026-10-15-admm-numerical-rejection/SUMMARY.md`.

## Fixed-contact ADMM cache — 2026-10-15

Implemented an experimental 64-byte-per-slot GPU cache of normalized normals,
inverse-mass penalties, local weights and free relative velocities. It is rebuilt
after validation and before factorization/iteration, keeping arithmetic order and
the 64-iteration algorithm intact. Both modes retain the same compiled pipelines,
cache allocation/clearing overhead, ordered staging and active-index publication.
No production default changes.

Twelve CPU contracts pass. One frozen GPU batch completes in 2.59 s and preserves
five-buffer exact prior-control/mode/self-repeat parity on both captured packets.
NaN-poisoned cache reconstruction, nine exact candidate cache builds and inactive
zeroing pass. Independent f64 normalized cache errors are
1.781150097e-7/1.514985664e-7 against a separate 2e-6 cache check. Physical and
numerical bounds remain 1e-6, public comparison remains 2e-5; the legacy old-public
failures remain recorded. All seven publication-index fault/recovery cases pass.

Paired total upper-median changes are +22.01%/+88.80%; total upper medians are
6.016000/5.987328 ms uncached versus 10.169344/11.269120 ms cached. Only 3/8 and
4/8 total pairs improve. Solve-only paired upper-median changes are -2.45%/+25.22%,
so even isolated solver improvement is inconsistent. External GPU processes were
left running and telemetry retained. No speedup or promotion is claimed; no
unchanged retry. Initial CPU compilation hit the JSON macro recursion limit;
splitting telemetry construction corrected it without changing crate limits,
and the failed source/log snapshot remains sealed under `initial/`. Evidence:
`benchmarks/soil/2026-10-15-admm-fixed-contact-cache/SUMMARY.md`.

The experimental standalone publisher now consumes the solver's ascending active
indices for machine rate and momentum reductions. Full input validation, contact
ownership, energy summation and zero-on-failure behavior remain unchanged.
Independent positive-mass counting plus ordered, bounded, active membership
validation prevents missing, duplicated or fabricated contacts from bypassing
certification. The production constructor still selects the original shader.

Eleven CPU contracts pass. A frozen 2.89 s RTX 4080 batch verifies two captured
251-active/4096-slot, 10-DOF packets: exact prior-control and mode parity for all

rejections plus exact recovery per packet without solver reexecution. All
physical/numerical and guarded-public gates pass; legacy old-public differences
of 0.003173800418/0.003193525248 still fail the unchanged 2e-5 gate.

Publication paired upper-median changes are -55.04%/-36.70%, with 7/8 pairs faster
in each case. Total paired upper-median changes are -37.35%/-15.17%, but ranges
are -82.10%..+363.51%/-74.61%..+287.99%. Total upper medians change from
18.269184/7.942144 ms to 5.725184/8.090624 ms. External GPU applications remained
running and telemetry was retained. This is promising component evidence, not a
reliable overall speedup, production acceptance or normalized frame timing.
No unchanged timing retry. Evidence:
`benchmarks/soil/2026-10-15-admm-active-publication/SUMMARY.md`.

Seven CPU contracts pass. Both captured cases have exact active indices, exact
five-buffer equality between modes and to the original FP32 control, and nine

One frozen RTX 4080 batch completes in 5.24 s. Eight alternating GPU-timestamp

medians remain 31.784960 / 34.316288 ms (full scan 100.703232 / 88.141824 ms).

6.259712 / 6.903808 ms. Phase medians are independent statistics, not additive.
Raw samples vary substantially; contention telemetry is retained. No comparison
to Newton speed or full-frame performance is established.

Intervals include validation, solver state clear, optional list construction,

All five buffers repeat exactly three times. Old-Newton public deltas
0.003173800418153405 / 0.003193525248207152 still fail 2e-5 and are retained.

## Low-rank ADMM contact reference — 2026-10-15

Implemented a test-only contact-space split motivated by
[Frictional Contact Solving for Material Point Method](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.02038v1),
not a replacement backend, compliant contact model or implicit-MPM implementation.
The linear response is constant within the captured contact problem. Analytic
contact/wall block inverses plus a Woodbury correction require one machine-sized
pivoted factorization. Coulomb-cone and signed wall-ray projections retain the
De Saxce normal correction. Captured prepared responses are not symmetrized.

The initial dense implementation passed its two CPU contracts but rejected the
first replay at its 128-active-contact cap. Both actual packets have 251 positive-mass
contacts in 4096 slots and 10 machine DOFs; 24 in their solver report is a count of
linear iterations. That terminal failure is sealed separately. The changed
block-local/low-rank implementation avoids a 1506-by-1506 matrix rather than merely
raising the dense cap. Its retained algebraic storage scales with contacts times
machine DOFs plus the small core. Diagnostic admission follows the packet bounds;
tested actual coverage is these two 251-contact inputs, not all admitted sizes.

Three CPU tests pass: pivoted reusable solves, cone/analytic-contact laws, and
low-rank versus full shifted solves on wall/no-wall and asymmetric-response
fixtures at 1e-12. Both authenticated packet replays run from explicitly zero
initial guesses through a CPU-only branch before engine construction. Each uses
one 10-DOF factorization and exactly 64 ADMM iterations with no penalty sweep.
The 30-second CPU cap is unchanged; both diagnostics finish in about 0.01 seconds,
which is neither GPU timing nor integrated physical-time performance.

**Both mechanism gates fail.** Independent mass-based physical errors are
6.875540931872116e-6 / 6.955646774219088e-6 against 1e-6. Prepared-response errors
are 6.875541089848999e-6 / 6.955646652346912e-6. Impulse differences from captured
state are 0.0006781329187649059 / 0.0006821590245154815 against 2e-5. Rate differences
of 1.3209594127205904e-5 / 1.3138230894993441e-5 alone do not override those failures.
CPU repeats are exact. Final normalized split residuals remain about 0.0108 primal
and 2.3e-6 dual. The audit reports diagnostic completion with zero mechanism passes,
not algorithm acceptance or the full GPU five-buffer/publication gate.

No GPU trial, production solver/default change, iteration-cap increase or tolerance
relaxation follows. Further work needs a justified convergence mechanism, not a
constant sweep or unchanged replay. Full 4 ms/60 FPS, trajectory, sleep/support,
traversal, rendered agricultural and calibration acceptance remain open.
[Failed dense admission](benchmarks/soil/2026-10-15-admm-contact-reference/SUMMARY.md);
[low-rank implementation and evidence](benchmarks/soil/2026-10-15-admm-low-rank/SUMMARY.md).

## Batched selected index paths — 2026-10-15

Production selected v2 publication applies its sorted unique edits in one recursive
radix traversal. The updater reads each affected old page at most once, retains
unmodified subtrees and writes each final changed page at most once. Leaf merges
use the sorted builder; new compressed-prefix ancestors and empty-child collapse
preserve ordered authenticated bounds and counts. No whole-field cache/map is
introduced. Updater scratch scales with selected edits and the 192-bit key depth.
These read counts exclude publication preflight, selected payload reads and backend
collision checks. Successful batches avoid intermediate orphan pages; failed
construction/publication can still require the existing validated collection.

Sorted uniqueness/nonzero counts are checked before page I/O. No-op batches retain
the old root. Mixed insertion/deletion can avoid a transient split retained by the
serial algorithm, so universal root-hash equality is not claimed: exact sorted
contents, totals and physical archive state remain required. File format, HEAD
publication barriers, poisoning/reopen and generation/read-token behavior do not
change. The former serial update path is now a private cfg(test) reference, not a
public production mode.

For 32 adjacent changed keys over 64/1,024/4,096 tiles, updater reads fall from
64/192/256 to 2/6/8. Page bytes fall from 68,096/92,672/104,960 to
2,128/2,896/3,280 with exact root hashes on these value-only fixtures.
The integrated same-build 4,096-tile comparison changes all four selected tiles
for each of 64 updates: serial writes **988,672 bytes**, batched **358,912 bytes**,
including payloads/index pages/HEAD. Exact final archive parity, periodic reopen
and GC pass. The earlier fixture changes only one selected tile and stays at
269,056 bytes; migration stays at 272,648 bytes. These are logical counts on
temporary storage, not disk latency or soil-frame performance.

**95 CPU store tests plus two admission/dispatch checks pass.** New checks cover
2,048 deterministic mixed edits against both a BTreeMap and the serial reference,
unique page reads/writes, final reachability, old-root retention, signed extremes,
deep prefixes, empty/full deletion, no-ops, malformed input/count overflow,
corrupt touched pages and failure at every page write. Existing publication cuts,
process-exit/reopen, poison and corruption suites also pass.
Eighteen frozen RTX 4080 live persistence/transition suites pass in **27.02 seconds**,
below the unchanged 90-second cap. No shader, numerical gate, physical sleep/wake
authorization, full traverse or 4 ms/60 FPS acceptance follows.
[Reproduction and sealed evidence](benchmarks/soil/2026-10-15-store-batched-paths/SUMMARY.md).

## Streaming index construction — 2026-10-15

Production v1-to-v2 migration and v2 full replacement now use a sorted streaming
radix builder instead of publishing each intermediate insertion path. It retains
one bounded leaf and an unfinished right spine; split bits increase strictly over
192 key bits. Completed left subtrees need no builder reads or rewrites; the file
backend still verifies existing hash-addressed files before reuse. Successful
construction writes only pages reachable from the final root, with the same exact
root descriptor/hash as the previous sorted-insertion algorithm. Selected path
updates and all durability, failure/poison, generation/token and format contracts
are unchanged. Failed construction can still leave unpublished pages for explicit
validated collection. Migration/full replacement remain field-sized enumerations.

For 4,096 sequential/random keys, builder reads are zero and final page counts are
255/355. Page-write bytes are 272,192/282,592 versus 6,996,992/7,039,312 for the
reference insertion implementation. These component fixtures have different key
layouts from the integrated field fixture; their byte totals are not interchangeable.
The identical integrated 4,096-tile migration drops from **6,873,544 to 272,648
logical bytes**, including its 456-byte HEAD. Its next 64 four-particle updates
remain at 269,056 bytes and preserve exact final archive/history bits. These are
logical write counts on temporary storage, not disk latency or a soil-frame gain.

**90 CPU store tests plus two admission/dispatch checks pass.** Tests cover root
parity, reachable-only writes, signed extremes and deep prefixes, malformed and
failing streams, injected failure at every page write, preservation of old roots,
migration/edit publication cuts, corruption, collection and recovery.
Eighteen frozen live RTX 4080 persistence/transition suites pass in **26.72 seconds**
under the unchanged 90-second cap, including upgraded raw/framed/canonical owners.
No numerical/shader/default-backend change, physical calibration, long-traverse or
4 ms/60 FPS acceptance follows.
[Source, independent audits and sealed evidence](benchmarks/soil/2026-10-15-store-sorted-builder/SUMMARY.md).

## Integrated incremental root publication — 2026-10-15

Promoted the verified radix-page implementation into production with an explicit
`upgrade_index()` operation on raw/framed/canonical stores. New stores remain v1;
open recognizes v1 and v2. Upgrade requires a committed store, streams its validated
v1 entries into pages and increments generation, staling previous read tokens.
Repeated upgrade is write-free. Older v1-only binaries reject upgraded roots; no
transparent backwards-reader compatibility or downgrade is claimed.

The v2 root contains generation, family metadata, archive totals and an authenticated
root descriptor. Public reopen validates every reachable page, ordering, prefix,
hash and aggregate before exposing the store. Selected updates reuse that validated
immutable generation under the private-directory contract. They install/synchronize
new pages before the existing ChunksSynced barrier, then synchronize a bounded root,
validate its exact candidate descriptor, atomically rename HEAD and synchronize the
directory. All existing post-publication failure/poison/reopen semantics remain.
No full-tree rescan is performed per selected publication; full replacement remains
an explicitly field-sized operation.

The shared manifest interface routes selected reads, iteration, cached totals and
workers for every storage family. Full collection validates the current archive and
tree before deleting unreferenced regular `.tile` and `.index` files. Publication
does not delete historical pages. The original migration produced intermediate
pages; the streaming builder avoids these, and the subsequent batch updater also
avoids intermediate pages on successful selected edits. Historical/unpublished
pages remain garbage until explicit collection. Root encoded-length accounting describes HEAD only,
not all index-page files. Newly written-byte statistics include pages and HEAD.

| Same 4,096-tile field, 64 four-particle updates | v1 | v2 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Logical changed payload/index/root bytes written | 15,781,632 | 269,056 |
| HEAD bytes | 246,120 | 456 |
| Original one-time migration bytes (before streaming builder) | 0 | 6,873,544 |

Final archive/history bits match exactly, with periodic reopen, bounded metadata
buffers and four retained cache entries after each update. The temporary store is
on tmpfs; these are logical I/O counts, not filesystem/device latency or GPU timings.

**87 CPU store tests plus two admission/dispatch checks pass.** New checks cover
uncommitted rejection, no-op upgrade, stale reads, partial/full/empty generations,
all storage families, root flags/digests/dimensions, corrupt referenced pages (including
an unselected subtree), cross-family and bound rejection, invalid existing page
installation, orphan collection/retry, and exact paired I/O. Upgrade and selected
edit each pass error injection and subprocess exit at all four publication barriers;
reopen chooses the complete old/new generation as appropriate. Process-exit evidence
is not hardware power-loss proof.

**18 frozen RTX 4080 suites pass in 26.84 s**, under the unchanged 90-second cap.
Includes existing persistence/retry/failure cases and upgraded raw, framed and
canonical live ownership: capture, overlap, stepping, transfer, activity, identity,
writeback, reopen and resume, with framed/canonical coverage across four grid modes.
No GPU rerun, physical algorithm change or numerical tolerance relaxation.
`make test-soil-store-incremental` is included in the S07 GPU aggregate.

[Design and sealed evidence](benchmarks/soil/2026-10-15-store-incremental-root/SUMMARY.md)
do not close physical sleep/support, bounded physical traversal, resource maintenance,
50k trajectory, 4 ms/60 FPS or agricultural acceptance. Batch migration/edit and
orphan maintenance remain opportunities; new-store migration is explicit, not default.

## Copy-on-write index page candidate — 2026-10-15

Implemented a private test-only incremental index candidate, not a production format
switch. It uses immutable BLAKE3-addressed pages and compressed binary radix branches
over sign-biased big-endian tile keys. Leaves contain at most 32 entries (1,936 bytes);
branches contain two checked child descriptors (192 bytes); backend reads use a fixed
2,048-byte buffer. Descriptors bind hash, key bounds and checked tile/particle totals.
Decode enforces strict ordering, child separation/prefixes, page dimensions, reserved
fields, version/hash and increasing split bits. A path is bounded by 192 key bits.

Insert/update/delete returns a new candidate root only after the required page writes
succeed; old pages are immutable. Full-leaf insertion splits at the first differing
bit, outside-prefix insertion creates a parent, and deletion removes empty subtrees.
No-op edits emit no pages. Sorted scan verifies referenced summaries, with a bounded
depth stack rather than a retained field map. Single-key edits can create intermediate
orphan pages; batching and explicit collection remain integration work.

| Field tiles | Pages read/written for one changed entry | Encoded page bytes written |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 64 | 2 / 2 | 2,128 |
| 1,024 | 6 / 6 | 2,896 |
| 4,096 | 8 / 8 | 3,280 |

The current 4,096-tile v1 manifest is 246,120 bytes. The candidate figures count only
index pages, excluding root/header publication, payloads and filesystem overhead;
they are not an integrated I/O or throughput result. Production integration follows
in the newer increment above; this candidate checkpoint itself was test-only.

**79 CPU store tests plus two admission/dispatch tests pass.** Six candidate tests
cover 4,096 deterministic random signed/extreme-key edits against BTreeMap, deletion
to empty, historical roots, no-op writes, page-size/path bounds, all intermediate
page-write failures with old-root readability and retry, maximum 193-page paths,
forged child summaries, count overflow, malformed/truncated/oversized pages and real
temporary-page reopen/corruption. The real-file adapter is only a page test backend;
it does not implement root transactions or directory durability. No GPU tests were
rerun for this cfg(test)-only candidate, and no prior GPU result is claimed for it.

[Design and integration contract](benchmarks/soil/2026-10-15-store-cow-pages/DESIGN.md)
records the remaining v1-compatible root format, validated migration/open, immutable
page installation, existing fsync/rename barriers, poisoning, garbage collection and
worker integration requirements. Synchronization requirements were cross-checked
against SQLite's primary [atomic-commit documentation](https://www.sqlite.org/atomiccommit.html);
this tree does not inherit SQLite's transactional guarantees. Full real-time and
physical acceptance remain incomplete.

## Storage accounting and fixed-working-set traverse — 2026-10-15

Added public `MpmSoilStoreStorageStats` exports and synchronous, I/O-free accounting
on raw/framed/canonical stores. Reports contain generation, archived tile/particle
counts, manifest encoded length, retained index buffer bytes, cached tile count and
cache limit. Failed stores reject until reopened. Ready disk owners delegate the
same accounting; pending/faulted owners reject rather than returning a stale
worker snapshot. The query takes no manifest lock and reads no file. Buffer bytes
exclude allocator/container overhead, file descriptors, OS page cache, worker stacks,
selected/captured payloads, transient publication buffers and solver/GPU allocations.

The storage-only worker traverse holds four selected particles while increasing
field size. Every tile is visited once, in a permuted order, with one particle's
velocity changed per window, reference-history comparison, asynchronous writeback,
periodic reopen and final full exact archive comparison. No particles are physically
stepped or declared asleep. The test oracle is field-sized and excluded from the
retained-store accounting; this is not an RSS measurement or physical-world traverse.

| Stored tiles | Updates | Index buffer bytes | Peak cached tiles | Peak selected read bytes | Logical bytes written |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 64 | 16 | 8,492 | 4 | 1,872 | 74,688 |
| 1,024 | 256 | 8,492 | 4 | 1,872 | 15,940,608 |
| 4,096 | 1,024 | 8,492 | 4 | 1,872 | 252,506,112 |

The v1 manifest is respectively 4,200/61,800/246,120 bytes, rewritten on every

**73 CPU store tests plus two admission/dispatch tests pass**, including accounting

**15 frozen RTX 4080 lifecycle suites pass in 22.14 s**, including ready raw/canonical

## File-backed manifest and bounded reuse cache — 2026-10-15

Replaced the authoritative production manifest BTreeMap with a validated open file
and bounded reader. Signed tile-coordinate binary search returns owned entries
with propagated I/O errors. Full enumeration collects keys explicitly to preserve
the public Result-of-infallible-iterator contract rather than hiding read failures.
Streaming enumeration checks the generation digest at completion. The caller-owned
directory must remain unmodified while open, as before; random lookups trust the
validated immutable inode, while selected blobs retain hash/count/metadata checks.

Selected raw/framed/canonical writeback no longer clones unloaded entries. It
computes retained counts through bounded affected-key lookups, streams the old
generation in sorted order, and merges the affected map into version-one pending
bytes. The writer validates order, counts, limits and cached totals. The synchronized
pending file is validated/opened before the existing publication barriers and rename;
the old descriptor remains valid through replacement. Unchanged generations skip
publication. Failure poisoning, original worker inputs and reopen semantics remain.

Reuse-epoch maps retain at most 1,024 entries, independent of visited field size.
Partial saves replace that cache rather than accumulating visited tiles. Eviction
only removes a reuse shortcut: a miss hashes/compares the existing blob. Full
save/load/enumeration/collection remain explicitly field-sized APIs. Changed HEAD
publication still rewrites and validates the full index; retained memory is bounded,
not disk work or worst-case latency. No storage throughput or physics speedup is claimed.

**71 CPU store tests plus two admission/dispatch tests pass.** New evidence covers
production index buffers at 1, 129 and 16,384 tiles, byte-exact merge versus the old
codec, deletion/insertion, old inode retention, unchanged publication, reopen,
malformed streamed order/count/totals, read-error propagation, and a real 1,025-tile
save/load/selected-migration/reopen with the cache cap and untouched reuse counts.
Existing crash-stage, locking, corruption, bounds and asynchronous ownership tests
remain passing. One frozen RTX 4080 run passes **14 GPU suites in 14.56 s**, including
raw/framed/canonical direct/background persistence and the nine transition lifecycle
cases, under the unchanged 90-second cap. No GPU rerun or gate change.

See [file-index evidence](benchmarks/soil/2026-10-15-store-file-index/SUMMARY.md).

## Worker disk transition admission — 2026-10-15

Moved the remaining disk-world transition manifest queries into owned workers.
Capture planning records bounded active counts and whether each requested tile
replaces an old selection tile. Before any writeback, the worker combines these
counts with unloaded tile counts, checks solver/particle/tile/encoded-byte limits,
and returns original inputs on rejection without poisoning a healthy store or
changing HEAD. After writeback, a worker filters absent region tiles before payload
reading. The caller bounds requested keys separately from actual nonempty tiles;
public strict reads still reject absent keys. Polling still performs bounded
particle bookkeeping and starts threads; this is not a hard latency guarantee.

Verification: **68 CPU store tests plus two admission/dispatch tests pass**. Paused
workers prove rejection executes off caller, retains exclusive ownership and
preserves HEAD and retry inputs. Existing-key reads verify deduplication, absent
tiles, independent request/payload bounds and canonical frame preservation. The
admission arithmetic covers replacement, migration into an unloaded tile, empty
tiles, both family byte bounds and lookup failure. One frozen RTX 4080 run passes
**nine GPU suites in 9.10 s**, including raw/framed/canonical capacity retries,
host/GPU swept pins, capture/write/load/reopen, publication failure and post-write
load failure. The unchanged 90-second cap includes GPU setup after Rust build.

An initial compile failure exposed a test-only store-count accessor removed with
the production caller path. The accessor is now test-only; its original failure
log is retained. No GPU retry or tolerance change. Full field maps and reuse-epoch
caches remain unbounded by active residency; physical sleep/support, long traversal,
full-frame throughput and trajectory acceptance are not established by this work.
See [sealed transition evidence](benchmarks/soil/2026-10-15-store-transition-worker/SUMMARY.md).

## Worker manifest preflight and cached totals — 2026-10-15

Separated bounded caller-side key preparation from manifest-dependent read
admission. Raw/framed and canonical background reads now deduplicate and enforce
the unique-key bound before spawning, without entry lookup. Canonical finite-frame
validation remains on the caller. Inside the worker, membership, particle and
encoded-byte bounds are checked before invoking the payload reader. Unknown keys
and manifest-dependent limit failures can therefore complete asynchronously, with
the original healthy store and unchanged generation. Thread creation and input
deduplication are not hard-deadline operations. Existing single-flight ownership,
file locking, spawn/disconnect behavior and panic poisoning remain intact.

Added `total_particle_count()` to raw, framed and canonical stores. The cached
aggregate is computed from verified records during open or publication and checked
against records during streaming writes. None means no committed generation; a
failed handle rejects access. Disk-world construction now reads this aggregate
instead of enumerating all stored tiles and summing per-tile metadata. The value
is committed metadata, not a claim about active GPU particle count or physical
mass. Version-one manifest bytes are unchanged.

**64 CPU store tests pass** in 0.12 seconds. New paused-worker fixtures prove that
unknown-key and particle/encoded-byte failures are deferred until worker admission,
never reach payload readers, retain the exclusive lock, return healthy owners and
leave HEAD unchanged. Existing immediate key/frame rejection, spawn/panic/drop and
publication regressions pass. Aggregate tests cover uncommitted, full save, movement,
reopen, empty replacement, failed publication and recovery; family accessors and
streamed cached-count mismatch rejection are checked too.

Six frozen RTX 4080 GPU suites pass in **8.43 seconds** under the unchanged
90-second cap: raw/framed/canonical persistence and background reload/resume plus
both identified live world owners. No shader, solver algorithm or numerical gate
changed. Source/executable/harness/fixture hashes surround execution and prior
sealed evidence is verified. This is not whole-frame speed or bounded-field
acceptance: the full entry map, partial-publication clones, reuse-epoch map and
disk-world transition count preflight still require migration before bounded disk
lookup can replace the authoritative map safely.

## Streaming manifest foundation — 2026-10-15; earlier migration checkpoint

Production store open and publication no longer allocate complete encoded HEAD
byte vectors. The version-one fixed-record format is read/written using 8 KiB
buffers, with at most 1 KiB retained metadata in the file-index foundation. Open
checks regular-file type, dimensions, generation, strict signed coordinate order,
nonzero per-tile counts, total particle bounds, digest, family and exact length.
The current adapter then materializes the existing BTreeMap and verifies the
entry digest again, detecting mutation between validation and materialization.
Publication streams into the same exclusive pending file, backpatches the digest,
flushes and fsyncs before the existing atomic rename/directory-fsync barriers.
Logical written bytes and version-one bytes remain unchanged.

The file-backed binary-lookup prototype uses a mutex-protected buffered cursor;
concurrent queries cannot corrupt the shared file position. Tests compare streamed
bytes against the legacy encoder and materialized maps at 0, 1, 129 and 16,384
entries. Buffer capacity stays fixed at at most 8 KiB plus 1 KiB metadata, excluding
fixed object/allocator overhead; this is not a process-RSS measurement. Bounds,
bad ordering/counts, digest damage, truncation, inter-pass mutation, symlinks and
wrong archive families reject. Existing selected-writeback, crash-publication,
locking, corruption, background-task and canonical/framed contracts also pass.

**60 CPU store tests pass** in 0.11 seconds. Five frozen RTX 4080 GPU persistence
suites pass in **6.65 seconds** under the unchanged 90-second cap: raw reload and
resume, framed direct/background reload and resume, and canonical direct/background
reload and resume. No shader or physics algorithm changed. Production solver and
facade builds are checked separately; source/executable/harness/fixture hashes
surround the GPU run.

The complete entry map is **still retained in production**, selected writes still
clone unloaded entries, and the epoch-reuse map still scales with history. Initial
open currently performs two entry passes; changed publication remains O(field)
I/O. The next stage must integrate the file-backed index and streaming merge,
bound reuse caching, expose cached total counts instead of whole-field enumeration,
and move selected disk preflight into workers. The increment above implements the
cached total and background-read preflight prerequisites. Simply replacing map.get with disk
I/O would violate the current nonblocking caller contract. No bounded-traverse,
whole-frame speedup or 4 ms/60 FPS acceptance is asserted.

Run `make test-soil-store RELEASE=1`; GPU reproduction uses the frozen checkpoint
runner with its unchanged aggregate deadline. [Migration source and evidence](benchmarks/soil/2026-10-15-store-manifest-stream/SUMMARY.md).

## Nonblocking quiescence acquisition — 2026-10-15

Added public quiescence request/poll/cancel on both soil owners. Blocking reads now
share the same bounded staging slot; overlapping reads return backpressure rather
than remapping or reallocating it. Pending metadata captures request-time identity,
epoch, attempt and byte count. Poll uses nonblocking device progress and a channel
try-receive; it decodes directly from mapped bounded words without an intermediate
word-vector copy. Cancellation discards provenance and drains completion before
reuse. Map/poll failures poison reads until disable/reprepare; completed metadata
faults return errors while releasing the slot. Physics and observation shaders,
GPU allocation budgets and numerical gates are unchanged.

Six CPU contracts and eight frozen RTX 4080 GPU suites pass in **16.72 seconds**
including setup, under the unchanged 90-second cap. Dense/active/compact grids
match blocking snapshots exactly. Coverage includes one-shot completion, busy-slot
rejection, invalid bounds/foreign engine, cancellation across dt changes, stepping
and cancelled encoding after request, actual identified restore to different global
IDs, reseeding to a smaller population, metadata faults, disconnected callback,
disable/reprepare, queued owner drop and explicit logical-device destruction.
Destroying this test-owned logical device is not a hardware-failure injection.

Both public owners now compose asynchronous quiescence acquisition with direct,
closure, ID-retention and region support requests. They preserve particle/material
IDs and reject requests, polls and cancellation during an owner transition. A no-op
region transaction explicitly takes the Unchanged transfer path and preserves the
queued snapshot's validity; the next physical step makes that result stale. Real
restore/ID replacement preserves the original request's IDs/payload/epoch in the
returned historical result and fails current-state validation. This corrects the
initial test assumption below; production source is byte-identical between the
failed and passing checkpoints. No provenance validation was relaxed.

For 129 particles, the bounded request/poll path records **zero hot GPU-buffer
allocations, zero uploads, zero dispatches and 1,048 readback bytes**. Retained
quiescence storage stays 2,080 bytes. Physical checkpoint bytes are unchanged.
These counters exclude host/driver allocations and do not establish a whole-frame
speedup. The APIs close blocking-only observation acquisition, not automatic
scheduling or physical sleep/wake/support. Continuous stepping can make any host
observation historical; current-state admission still requires validation. Full
integrated accuracy, bounded traversal and 4 ms/60 FPS acceptance remain open.

Run `make test-soil-quiescence-async RELEASE=1 RUN_WITH=nixVulkan` in the repository
environment. Solver/facade production GPU builds pass. The earlier failed run is
sealed and verified, alongside frozen source/executable/harness/fixture hashes.
[Passing provenance evidence](benchmarks/soil/2026-10-15-quiescence-async-provenance/SUMMARY.md).

## Nonblocking direct support observation — 2026-10-15; earlier checkpoint

Added public direct-support request/poll/cancel APIs on `MpmSoilWorld` and
`MpmSoilDiskWorld`. The existing support staging buffer is reused; the logical GPU
budget remains `80 + 4 * grid_size^3 + 8 * max(particle_capacity, 1)` bytes.

blocking readers share the slot, reject while occupied, and do not make an extra
provenance clone. Physics and query shaders are unchanged.

and lets nonblocking polling drain map completion before reuse. Cancelled results

physics/configuration/identity epochs. Neither result nor cancellation authorizes
sleep, support removal or particle eviction.

poll path. The initial GPU run then exposed incorrect classification after

The repair follows the existing checkpoint/surface drain-before-reuse pattern,
with explicit quiet-streak and blocking-threshold controls; no gate was relaxed.

completion, backpressure, cancellation/drain/reuse, validation before transfers,

Public memory/disk owner checks include stable particle IDs, foreign-snapshot
rejection and region-transition exclusion. Existing dense/active/compact direct,
closure, clipped-stencil and unchanged-physical-state regressions also pass.

For the three-particle direct request plus polling/backpressure checks, counters
observe **zero hot GPU-buffer allocations**, two dispatches, 64 uploaded bytes
and 28 readback bytes. GPU scratch remains 17,496 bytes for capacity 129/grid 16.
These counters do not claim zero host allocation or measured end-to-end speedup.
Actual device loss was not injected; disconnected callback and metadata faults
were. Closure, retained-support and region-support APIs were still blocking at

## Capture-time certificate provenance and early replay rejection — 2026-10-15

Fixed the missing certificate-version provenance that allowed costly exact-report
replays against incompatible metrics. The capture shader writes tag 1 for
`gap-independent-velocity-v1` into reserved packet header word 10. Export reads
that captured tag to emit `certificate_version` and `certificate` metadata.
The existing packet digest covers the tag. Header format and payload sizes are
unchanged; remaining reserved words stay zero. No physical state, arithmetic,
threshold, capture allocation or ordinary stepping behavior changes.

Tag zero means unspecified rather than an inferred old/new metric. Legacy input
and state analysis remains available, and legacy export explicitly retains zero.
Unknown versions reject before output-directory creation. Exact-success replay,
seed-cost comparison and first-release comparison require the current version,
matching metadata and packet provenance. There is no override that silently
retags old data or ignores the existing exact gate. Future certificate semantic
changes require a new version; this is explicit versioning, not an automatic
hash of every arithmetic expression.

Replay preflight bounds packet/metadata reads, validates digest and dimensions,
and checks certificate agreement. Batch mode preflights every packet before
constructing its shared GPU engine; individual replay validates before its own
GPU construction. Seven CPU cases cover current/legacy compatibility, malformed
metadata, unknown tags, missing/partial fields, reserved header bytes, shape and
digest errors, read limits, shader-tag agreement and the gap-independent formula.

same-solve seed captures retain their previous byte/latching/resource checks and

## Newton barrier folding and stale certificate baseline — 2026-10-15

Implemented a test-only protected-SPIR-V transform that removes an identical
barrier only when all intervening instructions in the same straight-line block
are invocation-local or immutable. Calls, control flow, shared/storage memory
accesses, memory operands and unknown instructions conservatively break the
candidate span. Two CPU contracts pass, including memory/control hazard fixtures,
idempotence, validated generated binary and equality of every non-barrier word.
The current solver has two eligible sites out of 190 static barriers: one in
`krylov_cycle`, one in `hybrid_direction`. No source arithmetic, branch, binding,
buffer or iteration limit changes, and production selection remains unchanged.

The candidate first-packet replay completes three bit-identical executions but
fails the archived report at word 5 after 65.69 seconds. A separately frozen
unmodified current control does the same after 65.83 seconds. Both remain below
the unchanged setup-inclusive 90-second GPU cap; both exit 101. Original and
candidate SPIR-V artifacts are identical across these two builds, and the only
common source-file difference is diagnostic collector labeling. All five output
buffers match between arms: state, rates, outputs, solver report and publication.
Archived state/publication remain exact. Independent physical error is
2.555279284772259e-7, below the unchanged 1e-6 gate. The second candidate packet
and performance acceptance were not reached; no speedup or promotion follows.

Comparing the actual frozen October 13 source with current source identifies a
certificate-contract mismatch. The archived `physical_error` used
`1 + length(soil) + length(machine) + gap` as velocity scale; the October 15
gap-independent certificate repair deliberately removed the gap term in both
GPU and CPU code to prevent false physical acceptance. The archived independent
error was 2.495473787974256e-7. This is a changed metric on unchanged physical
state, not evidence that the barrier transform caused the observed discrepancy.
It also corrects the earlier control-snapshot investigation's speculative
compiler-attribution direction: the stale baseline must be addressed first.

Both failed archive gates remain failed and sealed. Next work is capture-time
certificate provenance and a pre-GPU compatibility check, followed by separately
frozen current-contract controls. Do not rewrite legacy reports, relax numerical
bounds or infer full acceptance from candidate/control equality. The dominant
contact-solving cost, safe sleep/wake and full 4 ms/60 FPS goal remain unresolved.

Evidence: [candidate](benchmarks/soil/2026-10-15-newton-barrier-fold/SUMMARY.md),
[unmodified control and source diffs](benchmarks/soil/2026-10-15-newton-barrier-control/SUMMARY.md).

## Frontier-only support propagation — 2026-10-15

The production support closure now avoids gathering nodes for already reached
particles and scatters only particles reached during the current round. Node
search returns at its first positive flag. A temporary per-particle frontier bit
is cleared by the scatter pass, preserving existing result words and final
fixed-point validation. No new buffers, bindings, dispatches or readbacks are
introduced, and physical stepping/residency policy is unchanged.

The test-only original shader matches the prior sealed production SHA-256
`d7ea38d11cb85a176ae694435309d658a9bafa7fb31cab40b2625bcbdcae9dee`.
Forty-four differential cases compare every result and every node word across
29, 129 and 50,000 particles. They cover all-quiet, distributed nonquiet, one/two
explicit seeds, incomplete propagation, clipped particles and multiple round
limits through 64. Thirty-two small cases also match an independent CPU graph
implementation. Temporary frontier bits never appear in published results.
The separate existing suites preserve exact physical checkpoint bytes and
owner/resource/lifecycle behavior on dense, active and compact layouts.

Six alternating-order timing pairs on the 50k/64-round seeded fixture remain
bit-exact. Nearest-rank wall p50 is **1.853383 ms original / 1.429533 ms frontier**,
an observed **22.87% reduction**. Individual original samples range
1.739863–1.980887 ms; frontier samples range 1.361865–1.522972 ms. Both ranges
drift upward during the short run. Timing includes CPU command encoding,
completion waiting and diagnostic readback of results plus the full node field;
it is not isolated kernel time or simulated-time physics throughput. Before/after
telemetry reports 0% GPU utilization, but is not continuous contention evidence.

Six CPU contract/shader checks, 136 checkpoint regressions and facade/format
checks pass. All nine GPU suites finish in **15.00 seconds** on RTX 4080, exit
zero, within the unchanged setup-inclusive 90-second cap. Frozen source,
executable, fixtures and harness match before/after execution. No retries or
relaxed thresholds were used. Safe sleep/wake, bounded physical traversal and
the full tractor/implement 4 ms/60 FPS target remain open.

Evidence: [commands, scope and timing audit](benchmarks/soil/2026-10-15-soil-support-frontier/SUMMARY.md).

seeds and preserve physical checkpoint bytes exactly. They cover unions,

four-particle, two-round, one-box query records seven dispatches, 96 uploaded

Added stable-global-ID retention requests to both memory and disk live owners,
with a distinct `MpmSoilRetainedSupportSnapshot` exposing per-slot quiet,

soil and explicit requests, protecting quiet components containing retained

unchanged. Unknown/duplicate IDs, unidentified/stale boundaries, pending owner
transitions, and insufficient propagation budgets reject rather than producing

binding is added. Nonempty request lists cost 4 * live particle count extra upload
bytes; empty lists omit that upload. The existing parameter upload, readback and
dispatch bounds remain 64 bytes, 16 + 4 * particle count bytes, and
2 * rounds + 2 dispatches. Host mask/set/snapshot allocations remain explicit
and separate from the logical GPU byte budget. No ordinary-step work changes.

requires one global material ID. Initial source and failure are sealed. Source

dispatches, 80 upload bytes and 32 readback bytes. The six successful unchanged

This protects explicit retention dependencies; it neither establishes force
equilibrium nor authorizes sleeping or eviction. Machine/region seed generation,

## Exact transfer-tile reuse — 2026-10-15; opt-in, held-input gain

Added a retained exact-input P2G cache. Changed particles invalidate old and new
stencils; removed particles invalidate their former stencils; invalidity survives
inactive tiles. Configuration signatures cover origin, spacing and integer windows.
Unchanged tiles restore full mass/momentum/stiffness outputs into the current
physical storage mapping. Dirty tiles retain the original accumulation order and
arithmetic. All subsequent grid, contact and particle evolution still runs. No soil
support contribution is dropped, and this is not physical sleep or eviction.

The API budgets 176 bytes per capacity slot, 20 per logical node, eight per logical
4³ tile and a 64-byte header, excluding ordering/driver storage. It adds four storage
bindings and two dispatches, with no cache-path upload/readback. The retained node
cache is dense in the logical window, including for compact solver storage; large
unsupported windows reject rather than silently overallocate. Ordinary preparation
removes reuse; defaults remain unchanged. Explicit viewer selection is described above.

The first GPU run passed real evolution but failed three raw fixture diagnostics.
Its source/executable/logs remain sealed. Repairing active-grid/material uploads,
initialization and reseed material IDs changed **only the test file**. The repaired
run passes four tests in 8.90 s including setup, covering eight layouts/policies,
64 evolved exact checkpoints, 24 held exact transfers, removal/reactivation,
25 changed components per grid type, window shifts, faulted key publication and
actual cache-hit bypass. Seventeen CPU contracts, two existing stress-cache GPU
tests (6.00 s), formatting and facade compilation pass.

The separately frozen 50k detached fixture passes in 1.25 s, with 12 exact evolving
checkpoints and 12 exact held transfer pairs. Ten warmed pairs show:

| Measurement | Control median ms | Reuse median ms | Median paired change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Evolving P2G | 1.499136 | 1.554432 | +2.97% |
| Evolving sum of GPU stages | 1.701376 | 1.747456 | +2.08% |
| Evolving completed wall | 2.081651 | 2.108353 | +1.15% |
| Held-input transfer | 1.617408 | 0.170496 | -89.36% |

Reuse materially reduces unchanged-input transfer work but costs time when inputs
evolve. Keep it opt-in; do not promote or rerun unchanged timings to hide the
regression. The evolving lane spans only 0.0012 simulated seconds and the held lane
does not advance physics. This is neither a loaded tractor nor proof of the 4 ms
frame budget, physical sleep, bounded traversal, calibration or full-plan acceptance.

## Canonical sticking-node order — 2026-10-15; scoped reproducibility fix

The targeted repeat capture completes in 6.34 s: four separate-submission
controls and two composed arms, each advancing three steps. On the first step,
all six initial checkpoints and 27-node multisets are identical, but the four
controls produce two different states/rate vectors. Five node orders occur
across the six arms. Later input states can already differ and are not all
identical-input comparisons. This proves baseline non-repeatability, not an
exact batching pass. Raw node/spans/state/output files and an independent byte
audit are retained. The sticking gather uses atomic node append; the projection
then uses an order-sensitive 64-lane reduction tree.

Implemented `ordered-sticking-nodes` in the solver and facade. A per-body GPU
bitonic index sort orders all eight u32 payload words lexicographically before
the existing projection. It does not numerically recompute node values or
discard nodes, change body ownership, or weaken boundary/fault handling.
Equal payloads are interchangeable. Separate unsorted/sorted buffers avoid
in-place permutation hazards; shrinking/empty spans clear unused output slots.
The 64-lane workgroup sorts only the next-power-of-two live count. Shared storage
is `4 * next_power_of_two(capacity) + 8` bytes, with device limits checked before
allocation. Extra retained storage is `32 * bodies * nodes_per_body` bytes,
included in existing budget admission. The operation adds one dispatch, no
hot buffer allocation or host transfer. It is opt-in and independent of the
submission-composition feature; neither default changed.

Verification on RTX 4080:

- CPU WGSL/source/limit checks pass, including zero, overflowing and unsupported
  capacities. Independent GPU sorting passes two-body cases at capacities
  1/3/63/64/65/127/129/512/1024/4096 in 0.75 s, covering full/partial/empty spans,
  signed zero, payload ties, tail clearing, sticky fault/reset and hot resources.
- All twelve original exact comparison cases pass in 25.18 s with canonical
  ordering enabled in both arms: dense/active/compact × native/non-native ×
  sticking/unilateral, three evolving states and five output buffers each.
  Invalid/stale inputs still reject before hooks/uploads; hot allocations and
  readbacks remain zero. This does not relabel the old unordered failure.
- Ten late-particle-fault/rollback/retry cases pass in 8.88 s.
- Twelve dense fixed-face cases pass in 12.11 s; 24 active/compact fixed-face
  cases pass in 26.14 s. Existing independent rate, impulse, reaction, particle
  velocity and energy checks retain their original 2e-5 bounds.
- Compact overflow, stale-owner rejection, growth, empty reuse, pre-allocation
  budget rejection and domain scaling pass in 5.47 s. Reported single-body
  128-node ownership is 40,516 bytes for the tested compact pool, unchanged

## Projected submission composition — 2026-10-15; opt-in, acceptance open

Internal pre/post command hooks now compose the runtime's Jacobian copy/machine
guard, full projected soil schedule, particle-fault propagation, guarded machine
publication and load accumulation. `batched-soil-projection`, forwarded by the
`molla` facade, selects one submission for that sequence instead of three.
Default orchestration stays separate. Uniform writes remain per physical
substep; contact evaluation, iteration limits, arithmetic, profiling scopes,
material uploads, grid initialization and final fault checks are unchanged.
There is no cross-substep batching or additional GPU buffer allocation.

The first frozen test attempt fails in fixture setup (0.78 s): deterministic
gather is unsupported on the non-native dense layout. The corrected fixture uses
one particle there and 17 particles with deterministic gather on supported
native/active/compact layouts. The original failed archive remains intact.

The corrected exact matrix passes both dense non-native cases, including three
changing timesteps, device-produced input rates, post-publication copies, no hot
GPU allocations/readbacks, and invalid/stale rejection before hooks/uploads.
It then fails in 6.80 s on the non-native active-grid sticking case, third step.
The first two steps match all checkpoint streams, five output buffers and upload
counts exactly. The third step differs in APIC (max 1.6996638763e-8), velocity and
published machine rates (3.7252902985e-9), and elastic F (8.4983235726e-13).
Positions, mass, reference volume, log-Jp, material IDs, diagnostics, machine delta
and both status outputs remain exact. An offline raw-log audit records every
stream. These small differences do not pass the declared exact comparison;
later matrix cases were not reached. Atomic node append exists in the sticking
gather shader, but control-versus-control repeatability has not been measured
here and the divergence is not yet attributed to that ordering.

Separately, all ten existing late-particle-NaN fault/rollback/retry combinations
pass through the composed path in 10.19 s. They cover native/non-native and
ordered/gather variants of sticking/unilateral coupling: machine publication is
blocked on fault, checkpoint/history restoration is exact, and valid retry
publishes. The actual six-body runtime check reaches construction only, then
exits 124 at its unchanged 90 s cap. It is not an integrated pass and was not
retried. No actual50k timing or trajectory run was launched.

The feature remains opt-in, and `make test-soil-projection-commands` has known
failing exact/integrated gates. Submission-count reduction is implementation
structure, not measured wall-time improvement or fully resident acceptance.
Next: isolate reference repeatability on the captured failing case and verify
the real Newton runtime before any default promotion. The 4 ms/60 FPS,
full-trajectory, renderer-residency and physical-calibration gates remain open.

step-size and damping parameters are unchanged.

## Tire constitutive transpose bug — 2026-10-13; corrected production law

The GPU cofactor-column helpers were misidentified as inverses/adjugates. In all
three tire stress routes, a further transpose made the law use F^-1 rather than
F^-T. The single/atlas helpers are now named `inverse_transpose3` and used without
the extra transpose; the matrix-free helper is named `cofactor3` and divided by
its guarded Jacobian without transposition. The correct CPU row-major inverse
plus transpose is unchanged. No damping, timestep or material was tuned.

The independent oracle differentiates the existing compressible Neo-Hookean
energy (also documented in the [FEniCS hyperelasticity example](https://olddocs.fenicsproject.org/dolfin/2019.1.0/python/demos/hyperelasticity/demo_hyperelasticity.py.html)).
On 21 identity/rotation/shear/general cases, actual single/atlas node-force errors
fall from 2.33333349 to 6.9713336e-8; a probe of the matrix-free stress expression
falls from 14.0 to 3.5758598e-7. The unchanged scaled component bound is 2e-5.
This verifies the positive-J constitutive law, not a complete matrix-free solve.

Five GPU component groups pass in 0.54/0.69/0.51/0.50/1.10 s, including retained
vehicle/FEM equivalence, atlas routing, single-tet smoke and analytic bending
replay. The bending check now compares force preservation against the current
ordinary shader, rather than obsolete pre-fix forces, and explicitly rejects
nonfinite candidate/repeat/baseline outputs. Five CPU checks also pass.

One materially changed six-frame viewer recheck still fails the absolute 2e-5
trajectory gate, with maximum 20.1948957 (previous 2.1017861). Its direct references
repeat exactly; all five CPU fallbacks still match saved pre-frame inputs. The
2.29-second failure is retained, not rerun or hidden. It shows that correcting the
constitutive law alone does not stabilize the scene. Selection defaults remain
unchanged, resident cavity loads remain default-off, and analytic bending remains
private. This is no 4 ms/60 FPS, calibrated or rendered acceptance result.
[Frozen negative and corrected evidence](benchmarks/soil/2026-10-13-tire-stress-transpose-fix/SUMMARY.md).

adapted to this repository's vertex order. Gradient clipping remains 1e4.
Degenerate normals/edges and exactly flat hinges use a zero-gradient convention.
No production shader calls the candidate yet.

checks (maximum scaled derivative error 5.7204e-9). GPU gradients on those cases

error 9.0689e-7; GPU angle checks and two explicit degenerate/flat cases also pass.

velocity difference from 0.0056976974 to 0.0004167557. Position difference becomes
1.3411e-7; force outputs remain bit-identical to the saved ordinary outputs, and

The initial run failed opening a cwd-relative fixture before GPU math execution;
