Added `PreparedTireVehicleChassisStep` to the public kernel and facade exports.
Preparation retains the existing spin, suspension, wheel-row, brush, planar and
vertical pipelines, their immutable uniforms, packed wheel configuration and row
scratch. Spin, planar and vertical state buffers remain authoritative in the
existing owner. All eight independent parity combinations are prepared; the loop
does not assume their parities happen to agree.

`step` verifies engine health, native source identities, count, configuration bits
and physical owner properties before encoding. It executes six ordered compute
dispatches plus the retained brush's device row copy in one encoder/submission,
then advances all three CPU parity selectors. There is no hot GPU buffer,
pipeline or bind-group creation, CPU upload/download or wait. Command/suspension/
terrain buffer contents can change in queue order; wheel configuration now has
explicit refresh as described above. Fixed dt, terrain metadata or source
replacement require reprepare. Raw buffers/owner must
belong to the engine. Returned brush output is a retained mutable view. GPU
faults/device loss after submission are not atomic frame rollback; legacy raw
data/physics contracts remain unchanged.

Owned GPU buffer budget is `432*N + 436` bytes: 96N packed configuration, 112N
wheel rows, five 80-byte uniform records and the prior 224N+36 retained brush.
Four wheels require **2,164 bytes**, excluding existing owner states/maps, CPU
storage, driver memory and command-buffer allocation. Invalid budget/timestep/
count reject before new allocation. Other legacy vehicle APIs remain available.

Verification: two CPU contracts pass; three GPU fixtures including earlier
retained-brush regressions pass in **0.64 s including setup**, cap 90 s. The new
full-loop fixture exercises all eight initial parity combinations, four frames
each, with changing terrain and wheel commands. All **160 raw comparisons**
against the unchanged staged path match: brush output, planar, vertical, wheel
spin and suspension rows. All 128 wheel outputs have positive normal load and
finite forces, avoiding an unloaded parity-only fixture. The 32 prepared frames
encode exactly 192 dispatches and observe zero hot buffer allocations or logical
transfers; diagnostic reads and caller command/terrain changes are outside that
scope. Stale wheel configuration rejects without spin advancement; foreign owner,
foreign engine, insufficient budget, invalid dt and logical device loss reject.

This establishes resource/compatibility behavior for the existing brush vehicle
model, not calibrated traction, native Newton actual50k performance, full soil
coupling, viewer migration or long-horizon acceptance. No whole-frame speedup is
inferred from suite duration. Commands:
`make test-soil-prepared-chassis` and
`make test-soil-prepared-chassis-gpu RUN_WITH=nixVulkan`.
Evidence: [prepared chassis loop](benchmarks/soil/2026-10-13-prepared-chassis/SUMMARY.md).

## Retained brush consumer of GPU terrain — 2026-10-13

The existing `dispatch_input_buffer_resident` produced GPU outputs but allocated
new output/map/uniform buffers and uploaded CPU terrain on each call. Added
`BrushTerrainGpu` and `PreparedTireBrushTerrain`, publicly exported through both
kernel and facade APIs. It binds caller-owned height/friction maps directly,
retains the unchanged brush pipeline and bindings, and copies GPU-produced wheel
rows into fixed input scratch before dispatch. This handles changing producer
buffer identities without a per-step bind-group rebuild or CPU transfer.

The brush sampler is intentionally unchanged: its normal policy differs from
the FEM terrain-query sampler, so replacing it would change the physical model.
GPU wheel rows must satisfy the existing brush input contract, including terrain
mode. GPU map data and sampling coordinates remain under the existing finite/
valid-data contract; this path does not add the query API's per-sample status or
a physical fault latch. Raw buffers/encoders and vehicle-owner resources must
belong to the supplied engine. Native kernel context, engine health, count and
source-copy capacity are checked by the new path. Metadata validation and owned
byte-budget checks occur before allocation.

Owned buffers use `224*N + 36` bytes for N nonzero wheels: 112N input, 112N
output, 32 immutable uniform bytes and a 4-byte missing-map dummy. Borrowed maps
and driver allocations are excluded. Encoding performs one device copy and one
dispatch, with no buffer creation, bind-group creation, CPU upload/download,
submission or wait. `output()` returns a cloned retained handle whose contents
are overwritten on later encodes; callers needing history must copy it in order.

`step_resident_chassis_brush_owner_with_gpu_terrain` is an opt-in production
consumer: existing resident spin/suspension/row generation feeds the prepared
brush, and planar integration consumes its resident result before vertical
integration. It rejects prepared-count/engine/kernel mismatch before state
advancement. Legacy/default methods remain available. Other vehicle stages still
allocate and submit, and later-stage errors are not an atomic rollback contract.
This is not the native Newton actual50k tractor implementation or viewer migration.

Verification: CPU layout/budget check passes. Two GPU fixtures pass in **0.52 s
including setup**, under the unchanged 90 s cap. Flat, height and height/friction
cases match complete legacy output bytes. Twenty-four prepared encodes observe
zero hot buffer allocations and logical transfers, with exactly 24 dispatches.
Queued owner/map drop, zero count/budget/source-capacity rejection, foreign CPU
engine and logical device loss checks pass. A real resident chassis fixture runs
four changing-terrain frames; all **20 raw comparisons** of brush output, planar
state, vertical state, wheel spin and suspension rows match the old API exactly.
Mismatched prepared count rejects with unchanged spin state. This bounded parity
fixture does not establish loaded-wheel/agricultural traction acceptance.

GPU endpoints: RTX 4080 driver 595.91.07, 0/0% utilization and 9915/9914 MiB.
No latency gain or 4 ms/60 FPS claim follows from test duration or endpoints.
Commands: `make test-soil-brush-terrain` and
`make test-soil-brush-terrain-gpu RUN_WITH=nixVulkan`.
Evidence: [retained brush consumer](benchmarks/soil/2026-10-13-brush-resident-terrain/SUMMARY.md).

## Resident regular-terrain queries — 2026-10-13

Added public `PreparedSoilTerrainQueries` and `SoilTerrainSample` in
`molla-kernels` (also accessible through the facade's kernel exports). Preparation
binds caller-owned GPU vec4 query positions and the existing
`TireFemContactFeedbackGpuTerrain` buffers. The sampler reuses the exact existing
FEM height, finite-difference normal, friction, water, sinkage and velocity
sampling functions. It does not interpret a heightfield as volumetric MPM contact.

The query count and terrain parameters are immutable. Changes to count, scalar
parameters or source identities require reprepare; edits to contents are visible
in queue/encoder order without reprepare. The retained record owns its pipeline,
bindings and result buffer; bindings retain source resources. Raw buffers and
encoders must belong to the engine. Engine identity/device-health validation
precedes encoding; logical device loss rejects without CPU fallback. Consumers
must check each sample status and order reads after encoding. This is not a
timestamped asynchronous CPU observation or a fault-gated whole-soil snapshot.

Outputs are 64 bytes per query: normal/height, velocity/friction,
water/sinkage/nonnegative rolling-resistance scale, and status. Status x is 1 for
valid data, 2 for unsupported/nonfinite coordinates, 3 for invalid sampled data;
failed numeric payloads are zero. Untouched initial output is zero. Valid queries
use edge-clamped bilinear sampling and the FEM normal stencil. Stencil coordinates
must have finite grid-relative values with absolute magnitude <=1e9; spacing is
at least 1e-6. Required sampled raw map taps are checked before clamping so NaN
material values cannot silently become valid coefficients. Nonfinite output or
degenerate normal also rejects. This is per-query status, not a shared fault latch.

Preparation validates terrain buffers, dimensions, query capacity, dispatch/device
limits and `112 + 64*max(count,1)` owned buffer bytes before allocation. The 112
bytes are 96 immutable uniform bytes plus a 16-byte missing-map dummy. Borrowed
maps/positions and driver allocations are excluded. A prepared encode adds one
dispatch for nonempty queries, zero for empty queries, and no queue upload,
readback, application buffer creation, submission or wait.

Focused verification: one CPU layout/source-validator check; three GPU fixtures
pass in **0.64 s including setup**, below the unchanged 90 s cap. Coverage:
- 129 points including edge/outside positions times 16 optional-map combinations:
  2064 samples checked against independent height/normal/material/velocity oracles.
- Two encodes with an intervening GPU terrain copy preserve earlier copied
  output and observe the new height, including source-handle drop before submit.
- Real binned MPM compaction terrain export followed by query in the same encoder
  yields expected height, normal, sinkage and velocity. This exports the existing
  compaction-law raster, not the separately defined particle-centre envelope.
- Invalid coordinate/map status, zero payloads, recovery on later valid queries,
  budget/capacity/spacing/dimension rejection before allocation, empty dispatch,
  foreign CPU engine and logical device loss checks pass.
- Query encodes and the raster/query chain observe zero hot buffer allocations
  and logical uploads/downloads. These counters exclude driver/staging internals.

GPU endpoints: RTX 4080 driver 595.91.07, 75/0% utilization, 9915/9914 MiB.
No throughput claim is based on suite duration or those endpoints. Focused
commands are `make test-soil-terrain-queries` and
`make test-soil-terrain-queries-gpu RUN_WITH=nixVulkan`. Actual CPU-tire/viewer
consumer migration, remaining solver residency gates and 4 ms/60 FPS acceptance
are not closed by this interface.
Evidence: [resident query implementation](benchmarks/soil/2026-10-13-terrain-queries/SUMMARY.md).
The explicit facade re-exports were added after kernel evidence was sealed;
[export finalization](benchmarks/soil/2026-10-13-terrain-query-facade/SUMMARY.md)
records their source and compilation separately, with unchanged kernel code.

## Newton block initialization — 2026-10-13; not promoted

Inspection found that every nonlinear contact evaluation clears all 114 scratch
words before immediately rewriting the six residual words and, when linearizing,
24 direct and nine machine coefficient pairs. Added a test-only candidate based
on the admitted SoA profile. Valid linearizations clear only 12 unwritten direct
and nine unwritten machine pairs; the unchanged residual/block builders write
the remaining 72 words. Residual-only evaluation still clears the full block.
All rejected in-range contacts clear the full block before returning; the
out-of-range no-write return and downstream finite checks are unchanged.

CPU coverage proves every direct/machine coefficient is written exactly once;
the source contract reconstructs the original control exactly by reversing the
initialization changes. Both source variants compile through the protected
SPIR-V path. Control SPIR-V matches the admitted SoA candidate hash
`cc6fb8a18dcebb26e45a3d5b488499062bc5dfd800a659a20b009f2d20c8d1d9`.
No buffers, bindings, workgroup storage, dispatches, floating-point expressions
or iteration/tolerance limits are added or changed.

Release compilation takes 31.04 s; two CPU tests pass in 0.13 s. Eight paired
GPU cases complete in **75.86 s including cold setup**, cap 90 s. The two
overlapping program preparations take 73.694/73.849 s. All 40 candidate/control
and 40 archived-control public output comparisons are exact, 128 repeat checks
pass, and all 144 expected timestamp records are present. Maximum physical
residual is 8.042703606542908e-7; maximum public delta is zero. These successful
captured solves do not independently exercise every malformed-input branch.

## Fused/SoA actual tractor motion-fault recovery — 2026-10-13

Refactored the existing actual-tractor retry fixture to select fusion explicitly
per arm and added `tractor_50k_fused_motion_fault_exact_retry` under the SoA
feature. The original unfused test remains available. Two independent controls
remain unfused; the retry arm is fused. Live selection is asserted at construction,
after rejection and every committed frame. Manifest records requested arm modes
and the compiled SoA feature. Production defaults and solver limits are unchanged.

All worlds retain 50k particles, six bodies, five bindings, shared-chunk transfer,
4096 contacts, 1024 compact tiles, 34 substeps per frame and a 6,400,016-byte
motion guard. After three frames the fused arm switches to a zero bound and
receives a real first-substep motion fault on frame 4. Complete soil, four
persistent machine precision streams, six-body CPU state, time and counters
restore exactly; GPU render publication becomes invalid. Restoring the original
1 m bound and retrying recovers exact independent-control trajectories.

The test passes in **141.85 s including GPU setup**, with unchanged 180 s cap;
release compilation separately takes 30.58 s. All 66 committed-frame comparisons
pass across 33 frames per arm (99 digest records, 11 state streams per record).
Offline audits pass 50 saved raw comparisons and exact archived final soil.
Missing, duplicate and altered history negative cases reject. Source, executable,
fixture and harness hashes, scoped format, facade build and whitespace checks
pass. GPU endpoints: RTX 4080, driver 595.91.07, 0/99% utilization and 9914 MiB
at both ends. This diagnostic uses blocking state reads and is not performance
evidence. Later-substep actual faults and other fault classes remain open.

Evidence: [fused actual recovery](benchmarks/soil/2026-10-13-fused-tractor-retry/SUMMARY.md).

## Guarded particle proposal fusion — 2026-10-13

Implemented a production opt-in path that computes G2P and constitutive
projection consecutively in the same particle invocation, writing only the
existing 128-byte proposal. A separate commit dispatch still checks global grid
fault status before publishing any physical particle state. It does not scatter
the next grid and is not completion of the full G2P2G experiment.

`MpmSimulation::set_soil_motion_projection_fused`,
`RigidWorld::set_mpm_soil_motion_projection_fused`, and the tractor wrapper
prepare/select a retained pipeline without additional particle buffers. The
selection requires active motion bounds, remains dormant when bounds are
disabled, and invalidates prepared records only on changes. Projection-cache
selection rejects coexistence in both directions; quiescence commit observation
is supported. Direct and indirect publication encoding use the same selection.
Profile intervals are `guarded-g2p-plasticity` and `guarded-particle-commit`, with
unchanged query-count budgeting. Ordinary profiles and defaults remain unchanged.

The CPU source contract reconstructs the original guarded shader exactly after
removing the appended entry and reversing entry renaming; Naga validates it.
Production GPU-feature compilation passes. An initial Rust visibility error was
fixed before GPU freeze and retained as `visibility-compile-error.log`.

The particle GPU fixture passes **12 cases**: dense, active-dense and compact
explicit grids, plus compact implicit integration with two Jacobi sweeps, each
with sand/snow/viscous material. Each uses 129 particles across workgroups,
deformed F, nonzero plastic history and a fast last particle. Coverage includes
control self-repeat, byte-exact candidate checkpoint, two candidate repeats,
real motion-bound and invalid-plastic-history rejection with unchanged physical
buffers, recovery, stale prepared-record rejection, idempotent selection,
profile stage identity, reselection, quiescence and two-way cache exclusion.
The fixture finishes in **3.90 s** including setup.

Dispatch counts change from 6 to 5 (dense/compact explicit), 7 to 6
(active-dense explicit), and 10 to 9 (compact implicit). Retained guard storage
is unchanged at **16,528 bytes**; hot observed buffer allocations and logical
readbacks are zero. Fewer encoded dispatches are not a measured latency gain.

A public-world integration fixture finishes in **13.65 s**. Two unfused portable
dense direct controls and one fused retry world use matched motion bounds and
compensated reactions. Complete soil and all nine machine streams match at the
committed prefix/final boundaries. A real zero-motion-bound fault restores soil,
four retained precision buffers, committed CPU pose/velocity/time and frame
counters; failed GPU body publication is invalidated. The same-bound retry
matches both controls. This is a one-particle, two-substep-per-frame fixture,
not the 50k native-Newton workload or later-substep actual-tractor acceptance.

Both tests pass within one unchanged 90 s deadline. GPU endpoints show
0/43% utilization and 11244/11244 MiB on RTX 4080 driver 595.91.07.
Offline verification passes **12 checkpoint pairs plus 65 coupled raw
comparisons**. The original audit used a start-anchored grep and missed the
first result prefixed by the Rust test runner; it failed after both GPU tests
passed. An additive `audit.mk` corrects only offline counting, retains the frozen
original harness and validates existing artifacts without a GPU rerun.

This component evidence does not imply runtime-default promotion, actual 50k
acceptance, full G2P2G, rendered, long-traverse or calibrated physical acceptance.
The subsequent actual fusion comparison is recorded separately above.
Evidence: [guarded fusion](benchmarks/soil/2026-10-13-guarded-particle-fusion/SUMMARY.md).

## Field-major Newton scratch — 2026-10-13

Implemented the S06 layout candidate `soa-scratch`. The source transform replaces
private contact/inverse scratch addressing for every producer and consumer,
including nonlinear block generation, initialization/failure clears, matrix
products, preconditioning, direct/conditioned fallback and residual reads.
Residual scalars occupy six contact-major planes, direct pairs 36 planes and
machine pairs 18 planes; inverse coefficients occupy 36 scalar planes. Paired
components remain adjacent. The new allocation totals are unchanged: 456 bytes
per contact block and 144 bytes per inverse. No public output, input geometry,
history, solver limit, binding count or extra dispatch changes.

One CPU contract verifies complete nonaliasing address coverage at capacities
0/1/3/256/4096, unchanged binding/shared/private declarations and successful
protected SPIR-V compilation of both variants. The mixed replay retains early
archived-control validation and now requires all five candidate/control buffers
to match exactly before paired timings count. Both kernels prepare concurrently
using the final panic-safe cache; all solves and timings remain sequential.

All eight actual-tractor packets pass in **73.32 s including setup**, cap 90 s.
The two cold builds overlap at 70.959/71.321 s. Maximum independent physical
residual is **8.042703606542908e-7**, public delta zero under unchanged 1e-6/2e-5
bounds. Forty raw candidate/control buffers and forty control/archive buffers
match, with 128 exact repeats. Existing run-level zero buffer-allocation/upload/
readback and dispatch-count assertions pass. These scopes exclude construction
and explicit diagnostic observation; this is not a whole-application residency
claim.

The 144 timestamps produce sorted-hash paired median changes of -5.6286%,
-5.5254%, -3.7752%, -6.5997%, -5.3961%, -5.1359%, -5.0581%, -5.7479%.
Timing covers solver encode only, excluding reset/setup/readback. RTX 4080 driver
595.91.07 endpoints: 0/82% utilization, 9915/9650 MiB. No exclusive-access or
measured memory-transaction/bandwidth claim is made; addressing motivates the
layout, but the comparison does not isolate the hardware cause of its gain.

The candidate remains test-only. Its stable gains justify integration and actual
50k trajectory/performance evaluation, not automatic default promotion. Internal
AoS-dependent diagnostic readers/probes must remain explicit when introducing
runtime layout selection. Empty/sparse/nonfinite/fallback lifecycle breadth and
full tractor acceptance are not proved solely by this eight-packet corpus.
Full 4 ms/60 FPS, bounded physical support/wake/traversal and agricultural gates
remain open. [Frozen source, all comparisons and reproduction](benchmarks/soil/2026-10-13-newton-soa-scratch/SUMMARY.md).

## Bounded parallel program cache and paired Newton admission — 2026-10-13

Changed the production program cache from holding its mutex through compilation
to type/key reservations with a condition variable. Ready hits remain available
during unrelated cold builds; at most two builds run concurrently (one for a
one-entry cache). Ready LRU capacity stays 64 by default. Same-key builds remain
single-flight, failures/panics release reservations, and clear installs a new
generation without canceling callers' in-flight work. Old-generation results
return to their callers but are not retained after clear. Existing kernels keep
their own references. Initializers must not reenter this cache.

The paired test's opt-in parallel preparation creates both current control and
specialized candidate on the same logical device. Only construction overlaps;
warmups and all eight alternating timing pairs remain sequential. wgpu 29.0.3
uses thread-local error scopes with the enabled `std` feature. An actual GPU test
overlaps a valid and invalid shader creation, checks correct error attribution,
retained good handle, failed-key retry and healthy device state.

Initial verification passes eight cache CPU checks and five shader/source
contracts. Three GPU cache tests take 0.52 s; the full paired replay takes

setups take 70.716/71.892 s. All eight packets pass the independent physical gate

and 128 repeat checks. Subsequent offline raw checks confirm **40 exact

No exclusive-access, full-tractor or 4 ms acceptance claim follows.

Post-run review hardened destruction of retired entries: eviction now completes
reservation cleanup/unlocks/notifies waiters before dropping the retired value,
and clear detaches the old queue before dropping it. This prevents a panicking
destructor from causing double cleanup or poisoning the cache lock. The final
source passes **16 compute CPU tests**, including eviction/clear destructor
panics, and **three GPU cache tests in 0.52 s**. Its source/executable/evidence
are frozen separately; the previous paired timing belongs to its original
pre-hardening executable and was not repeated after this cleanup-only change.

assertion incorrectly counted two ordinary private lane-index loads as rounding
accesses; the failed log/source are retained and the corrected audit counts

construction begins but does not complete. No full solve, physical result, public

Added `RigidWorld::set_mpm_soil_motion_bound` and the `SoilTractor` wrapper.

## Exact Newton inverse reuse — 2026-10-13, rejected

Implemented a test-only lane-local exact inverse cache, distinct from the earlier
lagged preconditioner. The key contains contact identity and every bit of the
36 paired direct and 18 paired machine coefficients; rows and responses are
immutable within a solve. Only successful inversions are eligible. Cache misses
invalidate the key, clear the inverse, and call unchanged Schur/dense factorization;
failed builds retain the original identity fallback and report accounting. Changing
contact identity misses safely when one lane processes multiple contacts. Private
state starts invalid for every invocation; there is no cross-dispatch reuse.

No new retained GPU buffer, binding, workgroup array or solve dispatch is added.
The private key is 432 bytes per invocation before compiler allocation. Diagnostic
per-lane hit/build counters are exported into existing condensed scratch only after
the complete solve returns, then read outside timing. These counters are not a
production telemetry path. Both arms share one compiled pipeline and explicit
parameter selection. Source checks preserve inverse bodies, evaluation, hybrid
iteration schedule, preconditioning and final certification.

The CPU/compiler contract passes, followed by all eight frozen current-workload
packets in 66.23 s including GPU setup (Rust build 29.68 s outside the cap). The
five public output buffers match exactly between arms and archived method 30;
all 128 timed self-repeats pass. Independent maximum physical residual is
8.042703606542908e-7 against 1e-6; public difference is zero against 2e-5.
The candidate's observed counters report zero hits and 24,487 builds, matching the
control build total. The corpus does not exercise a positive cache hit, so this is
not a general cache-hit correctness proof or rationale to expand cache scope.

All eight paired medians regress, from 0.348447% through 0.907838%. Reject this
unchanged candidate. No production/default change or actual tractor rerun follows.
Before/after RTX4080 utilization is 0/88%, memory 9920 MiB both; no intervention or
continuous telemetry. Source/executable/fixture/harness/reference hashes bracket
the run, and artifacts are preserved. Physical and frame acceptance remain open.

Separately, the user was asked whether to authorize an opt-in CUDA solver prototype
alongside wgpu. The current CUDA Math API documents explicitly rounded scalar
addition/multiplication; using those instead of the current SPIR-V volatile rounding
relay is an unmeasured performance hypothesis, not proof of a WGSL limit. CUDA would
add NVIDIA-specific build/interop/maintenance costs. No new backend/dependency is
implemented while that decision is pending. Any approved work retains all frozen
gates and counts device interop costs. [NVIDIA primary reference](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-math-api/cuda_math_api/group__CUDA__MATH__INTRINSIC__SINGLE.html).

## Exact-rest snapshot provenance — 2026-10-13

Quiescence snapshots now retain private configuration and encoding provenance,
immutable observations and immutable global-ID mapping. Both owners validate
snapshots only while ready and healthy. Cross-owner snapshots, changed identity or
configuration, intervening encoded steps (even cancelled), pending transfers and
disabled observers reject. Zero-substep calls and reads preserve validity.
Mutable encoder access invalidates the observation epoch; a subsequent observed
step clears previous streaks. The encoding counter uses checked addition and
cannot wrap into an older valid snapshot. This adds no GPU buffer, dispatch,
upload/readback or per-step allocation. It does not validate future support.

one shader/layout check and **134 checkpoint regressions** pass. Coverage includes
129 particles in dense/active/compact layouts, both live owners, exact checkpoint
preservation, cancellation, submitted steps, restore, failure, overflow, and
cross-owner/pending rejection. Historical command-batch force-parity failures are
not resolved or waived. No sleeping, eviction, long-traverse or speedup claim.

## Per-substep exact-rest observations — 2026-10-13

Added optional GPU observation to the existing guarded publication dispatch.
Each physical slot retains a u32 exact-rest streak and dt bits. A successful
publication increments the streak only when both old/new velocity and affine C
are zero and position, elastic F and plastic-history physical components are
bit-identical. The count saturates at u32::MAX; a changed dt starts a new streak.
This is an exact discrete-state observation, not a calibrated sleep threshold or
an equilibrium/support certificate. Material/load changes and unobserved dormant
neighbors still require separate physical admission.

Both memory and disk owners expose `prepare_swept_quiescence(max_bytes)`,
`read_swept_quiescence(engine,max_particles)`, `swept_quiescence_bytes()` and disable.
Preparation requires a prepared swept guard. Observer records and retained readback
storage cost 16 + 16 * max(capacity,1) bytes separately from the guard and checkpoint
staging: 2080 bytes at capacity 129, 800016 at 50k. Explicit reads copy status and
8 bytes per active particle, validate device/health, and return an optional immutable
global identity mapping with the historical observations. Reads require exclusive
owner access and reject pending, stale/reset, disabled, faulted and oversized states.

Configuration/restore invalidation marks observer storage for clearing before the
next batch. Command-batch cancellation restores that pending-reset flag so discarded
GPU clears cannot make stale streaks readable. Index/material/identity transitions
remain conservatively invalidating. Normal observation adds no dispatch or physics
upload/readback; the optional commit shader updates records before publishing state.
The ordinary commit pipeline is unchanged when observation is disabled.

Final frozen root-Make verification:

- `test-soil-quiescence RELEASE=1 RUN_WITH=nixVulkan`: **3 passed in 2.13 s including
  setup**, with the original 90-second cap. Dense, active and compact 129-particle
  fixtures observe streaks 3 then 5, reset to 1 on dt change, reject cancelled/stale
  captures and recover after restore. A fault without configuration changes leaves
  the previously nonzero records exact, while public reads reject the fault.
- A zero-gravity exact-rest fixture preserves all physical checkpoint bytes; its
  prepared hot batch allocates no GPU buffers and performs no readbacks. This is
  not evidence that a gravity-loaded bed settles.
- Five controlled proposal/commit probes change position, velocity, C, F or plastic
  history and return the physical endpoint bytes to their initial state. The
  disturbed slot reports 0,0,1 rather than continuing the prior streak; the other
  128 slots continue to six. These are observer tests, not physical loading runs.

invalidation are applied. Coordinate recentering still uses its translated upload.

solver metadata.

including setup**, including existing recenter identity/reopen, fault/rejection and

give **48 zero-error physical comparisons and exact control repeats**; 144 framed

zero upload bytes**, and **20,656 bytes of required capture readback**. Durable
reopen is exact for each case. RTX 4080 driver 595.91.07 endpoints: 0/5 percent GPU,
5427 MiB both; storage ext4. No claim of zero readback, hot-path timing, long
traversal, sleep/wake, machine coordination or whole-frame acceptance follows.

It lacks an independent self-repeat control and per-step captures, so no cause

diagnostic contribution arrays, queue submissions or readbacks in the owner.

requires non-native two-pass scatter, a matching grid-buffer identity and matching
active/deferred policies. Enabled grid-mode/lookup changes and grid growth are
rejected until disabled; disabled stale owners must be prepared again. Existing
backend setters enforce exclusive selection. Particle count/material updates and
checkpoint restores retain the owner, while prepared parameter records follow

the original base shader hash and all default selections remain unchanged.

The owner is opt-in and no speed gain is claimed. The separately verified rounded

residuals join the global tail separately instead of being discarded by a rounded
local high-plus-tail flush. A final active-node dispatch resolves the high/tail
pair. No spinlocks or extra within-kernel barriers are introduced.

not claimed repeatable. Final sealing separately compares all six candidate
stiffness files to rounded gather, rather than inferring byte identity from zero

unrebased owners and one owner rebased from grid [-4,-4,-4] to [-5,-4,-4]. World

fixture proves detection of a 1.19209e-7 metre difference that absolute sums erase.

not silently enabled in the ordinary controls. Submission order alternates each
step. All 168 captured framed snapshots and 56 comparisons are retained.

| Transfer | Grid mode | Exact self-repeat | Rebase physical checks | Maximum rebase error |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Ordinary | Dense | 0/8 | 8/8 | 2.38419e-7 |
| Ordinary | Active | 1/8 | 8/8 | 2.38419e-7 |
| Ordinary | Sparse | 0/8 | 8/8 | 2.38419e-7 |
| Ordinary | Sparse, ordered index | 0/8 | 8/8 | 2.38419e-7 |
| Fixed-order | Active | 8/8 | 8/8 | 2.38419e-7 |
| Fixed-order | Sparse | 8/8 | 8/8 | 2.38419e-7 |
| Fixed-order | Sparse, ordered index | 8/8 | 8/8 | 2.38419e-7 |

Position differences are absolute metres; other floating stream differences use
max(1,abs(a),abs(b)) normalization. Material IDs are exact. The frozen threshold
is 1e-6 and self-repeat is bit-exact. The combined test **fails** because ordinary
P2G violates self-repeat, not because the measured rebase error exceeds tolerance.
Sparse index ordering alone does not provide deterministic physical accumulation.
This is evidence for using fixed-order P2G in further repeatable streaming work,
not default promotion or full-plan acceptance. Longer evolution, bounded traversal,
physical boundaries/sleep and full 50k performance remain unproven.

## S07 canonical live coordinate rebasing — 2026-10-12

`begin_recenter(grid_origin)` stages the selected canonical token in the requested
frame and starts an asynchronous checkpoint capture. `poll_region_update` checks
the actual captured particle/grid translation before any upload or owner change.

token together. No tile I/O or durable generation change occurs. The same device
IDs and identity epoch remain installed. Residency, activity duration and consumed
swept horizon remain intact; GPU pin buffers receive new local parameters on their
next submission. Region changes and stepping are blocked while capture is pending.

nonfinite inputs and lossy baseline assembly reject at preflight; actual captured
coordinate rounding rejects before publication and permits retry. Foreign engines
leave the pending request intact. Invalid captured physics faults the owner. Device
loss is not rollback. Selected host assembly, capture validation and full physical
upload are boundary costs; this is not zero-copy rebasing or a hot-step speedup.

## S07 canonical background I/O and frame assembly — 2026-10-12

Added typed read/write task and completion APIs. `begin_read` takes requested
tiles, payload bounds, world origin and grid origin; its worker loads canonical
records and assembles the exact selected frame. Completion returns the exclusive
store and either None for uncommitted storage or the canonical read/selection
pair. Conversion errors remain retryable without poisoning the store.

`begin_writeback` moves the store/read/selection/update into one worker and returns
all inputs on success or failure. Shared caller preflight checks provenance,
frame, count and source bounds without scanning particles. Worker work includes
particle validation, affected-destination bounds, canonicalization and publication.
The private owned-task helper uses bounded one-slot request/result channels with
no synchronous fallback or unbounded queue. Polling moves buffers and consumes a
completion once; a disconnected worker is terminal. Caught worker panics and
publication failures poison the owner. Task drop neither joins nor cancels work,
and the lock remains held until the worker finishes.

Release compilation passes in **26.50 s**. The S07 CPU lane passes **130 tests**
(8 vehicle, 121 checkpoint, 1 identity; 65 GPU cases ignored). Seven new lifecycle
cases verify worker-thread frame assembly, pending lock ownership, pointer-
identical result/input buffers, exact history, unloaded preservation, startup
failure, worker exit before request, frame/bound/conversion errors with retry,
read/publication error and panic health, complete published recovery, dropped
read/write lock behavior, empty reads and terminal disconnected/consumed polling.

**20 GPU checks pass** under one setup-inclusive 90-second cap: two canonical
store cases (**0.57 s**), raw store (**0.38 s**), two framed stores (**0.50 s**)
and fifteen disk-world regressions (**5.33 s**). The new 129-particle fixture
evolves soil, saves/drops/reopens, background-reads and assembles an alternate
exact frame, restores exact physical/history state and actual device-ID words,
resumes, background-writes and verifies the exact reopened archive. This is not
later independent trajectory equivalence, physical traversal or a frame speedup
measurement. Store/disk tests use the explicit ext4 root.

## S07 incremental canonical tile store — 2026-10-12

Added `MpmSoilCanonicalStore`/`Read`, exported through the facade. The store uses
the existing exclusive lock, manifest, synchronized blob installation, staged HEAD
rename and directory synchronization. Blob installation/publication/validated
collection are shared helpers; raw/framed encodings and synchronization order
remain unchanged. Canonical metadata distinguishes the family, so wrong-family
committed opens reject. Uncommitted directories acquire their family on save.

Full saves reuse unchanged tile epochs/blobs; full load validates the entire
field. Bounded reads load canonical payloads only, checking selected hashes,
counts, metadata, tile keys and global-ID uniqueness. `read.select` assembles an
explicit solver frame, and partial writeback requires both the current read and
its selection token. It checks selected invariants, bounds the affected source/
destination union, merges only needed destination payloads and preserves unloaded
entries. Read/validation failures remain retryable; publication failures poison
the owner and require reopen. Changed generations stale prior reads. The manifest
still scales with the field, and all new APIs are blocking.

Canonical I/O reserves **1052 bytes per affected/requested tile + 181 bytes per
particle**; this is a conservative encoded bound, not physical filesystem or
allocator usage. Raw/framed bounds remain unchanged. Subset encoding performs no
frame conversion and does not assemble the whole field. Patch copies are bounded
by selected/affected payloads, not zero-copy. Unchanged-epoch reuse does not reread
disk to detect damage. Selected operations do not certify unloaded integrity.

The first test build failed on a Debug requirement in one new assertion; retained
initial source/logs show this. The corrected assertion leaves production traits
unchanged. Release compilation then passes in **24.66 s**. The CPU lane passes

Six new cases cover save/reopen/zero writes, byte/count bounds, cross-family opens,
alternate-frame moves, untouched hashes, stale/foreign selections, nonmutating
validation failures/retries, unselected corruption isolation, empty state and
collection. Eight full/partial publication failures reopen complete expected
old/new canonical generations. Existing raw process-interruption tests pass too;
this is not canonical subprocess or power-loss certification.

**23 GPU checks pass** under one setup-inclusive 90-second cap: canonical store
1 (**0.34 s**), raw store 1 (**0.36 s**), framed stores 2 (**0.54 s**), disk world
15 (**5.00 s**), raw tiles 2 (**0.33 s**), canonical tiles 1 (**0.25 s**) and framed

reads selected canonical data, assembles another exactly representable frame,
restores exact physical/history/device IDs, resumes, partially commits the captured
update, then reopens the exact resulting archive. This is transfer/reload evidence,

## S07 canonical per-tile host archives — 2026-10-12

Added `MpmSoilCanonicalTileArchive` and `MpmSoilCanonicalSelection`, exported
through the facade. `MpmSoilFrameCheckpoint::partition_canonical_tiles` stores
each position relative to its world tile in f64, retaining all other f32 history,
padding and exact IDs. Signed-zero flags preserve position bits when a frame
offset converts original negative zero to a nonzero tile-local residual. This
does not increase physical simulation precision. Exact tile anchors and residuals
are required; unrepresentable conversions reject rather than round or coarsen.

Selection deduplicates requested tiles, checks particle bounds before assembly,
sorts by global ID, and converts only selected records into explicit world/grid
origins with exact f32 conversion. Unknown tiles and unsupported coordinates fail
without archive mutation. Selected-frame writeback validates provenance, frame,
configuration, mass, reference volume and material identity, canonicalizes updates,
merges destination records and then commits under a new selection epoch. Unloaded
tiles remain unchanged. Changing the supplied grid origin is an execution choice,
not a validated physical moving-boundary transaction.

The distinct `MOLLCTIL` v1 codec has a digest and bounded decode, explicit tile
keys, global IDs, f64 local positions, signed-zero flags and remaining f32 words.
Payload cost is **181 bytes/particle + 28 bytes/occupied tile**, plus bounded
metadata; old raw/framed formats remain unchanged. Metadata retains no particle
buffer. This host archive is not yet accepted by the incremental store/live owner.

Release compilation passes in **28.58 s**. The S07 CPU lane passes **117 tests**
(8 vehicle, 108 checkpoint, 1 identity; 63 GPU cases ignored). Six new CPU cases
cover tiny negative boundary offsets, signed zeros, all-history codec equality,

moved-particle merging, unloaded preservation, stale/foreign tokens, mass/volume/
material/configuration rejection, every byte truncation/one-bit corruption of

Unrepresentable decimal anchors and very small residuals explicitly reject.

## S07 split-coordinate tile membership — 2026-10-12

Added allocation-free `SoilTileLayout::tile_at_local` with exact floor semantics
for the represented local coordinate, frame origin, layout origin and edge.
A bounded floating expansion retains cancellation residuals; comparisons against
integer multiples of edge correct boundary-rounding errors without forming an
absolute position. Nonfinite inputs/intermediates and tile magnitudes at least
2^52 reject. The existing rounded-arithmetic `tile_at` contract is unchanged.

order without changing IDs or residency. Tests reproduce the lost negative
offset in `1e12 + (-1e-6)`, cover 3,960 scaled-i128 oracle cases, subnormal edges,
huge-origin cancellation, coordinate limits and 2,575 exact rebase comparisons.

conversion and the existing missing resource-counters test feature; both failures

audits pass. No GPU run or speedup is claimed. This is a coordinate foundation,
not canonical tile-local persistence, automatic rebasing or physical boundary
acceptance. The expansion approach follows

## Retained mass predictor — 2026-10-12, experimental component

The new public `ExperimentalMassPredictor` consumes row-major, exactly symmetric
SPD f32 mass matrices and paired drive/bias vectors for 1..32 generalized DOFs.
It retains its pipeline, bindings, paired output and sticky status. A single
dispatch performs f64 Cholesky and separate force/bias solves, verifies 1e-6
residual certificates, then publishes the complete result. Invalid input,
non-SPD factorization or failed solve/certificate leaves the previous result
unchanged. Reset clears only status; no regularization or production default
change is introduced. Newly allocated output is zero until a successful dispatch;
consumers must order dispatch before consuming the result and check status.

The RTX 4080 GPU contract passes in **0.43 s including setup**, under 90 s.
Width-1/32 fixtures cover known solutions, negative pivots, nonfinite M/drive/bias,
sticky faults, exact output preservation, reset, overflow and asymmetry. Every
encoded solve checks zero host transfers/observed allocations, stable retained
buffer/bind-group/pipeline counts, and one dispatch. The frozen biased six-body
fixture supplies independently CPU-assembled mass and Newton–Euler bias;
ten changing force inputs yield **1.933317139933302e-9** absolute and
**1.812664925308853e-8** incremental force residuals (<1e-6), and
**3.0733654024617204e-9** dt-scaled rate error (<1e-5). Twelve paired result
captures and source/executable/input hashes are preserved.

This is not live CRBA/RNEA integration, ordinary ABA parity or a speed comparison.
The old biased-ABA failure remains. The subsequent increment above implements
an experimental free-joint bias producer; control and constraint parity, operator
epochs/rollback, moving trajectories and actual 50k performance still need
implementation and verification. No calibration data
is available; latest actual full workload remains 554.870 ms median, not 4 ms.
[Evidence](benchmarks/soil/2026-10-12-retained-mass-predictor/SUMMARY.md).

### Independent incremental mass response — failing physical gate

An offline CPU oracle now builds a 10-DOF mass matrix from independent f64 body
COM Jacobians, the frozen fixture's masses/inertias and captured f32 body poses
lifted to f64. A pivoted Gaussian solve, not ABA or shader factorization, predicts
acceleration differences between the ten increasing force configurations.
Capture integrity, expected geometry, identical paired outputs and constant
physical input records pass. The standalone solve test also passes. Differencing
the fixed-state responses cancels ideal gravity/Coriolis bias, but samples only
one force direction and is sensitive to finite-precision cancellation.

The unchanged **1e-6 normalized incremental-force gate fails** at
**1.2850820506263895e-5**, identically for storage and native records. Maximum
acceleration difference is **1.143673176215998e-4**; multiplying by fixture dt
gives **5.60624139142974e-8**, below the separate 1e-5 rate-increment bound.
The worst force row is step 1 / vertical translation: absolute residual
**0.002197490306571126**, normalized by 171. Its conservative final-output
half-ULP bound is **0.0015834232908673584**, so final rounding alone does not
fully account for the discrepancy. These diagnostics do not relax the gate.

The original and diagnostic failures are retained. This does not identify a
native-induced regression, because the two records are exact; it requires
resolving the rounded-pose oracle interpretation and response arithmetic before
promotion. No GPU rerun or production acceleration change occurred.
[Oracle, assumptions and failure evidence](benchmarks/soil/2026-10-12-acceleration-mass-oracle/SUMMARY.md).

### Absolute Newton-Euler balance — corrected fixture, scoped pass

A separate independent f64 oracle projects body forces and torques through COM
Jacobians, including gravity, root-angular centripetal acceleration, transported
wheel spin and world-inertia gyroscopic torque. It does not use ABA or subtract
gravity-biased GPU accelerations. Unit contracts cover static gravity, zero bias,
quadratic velocity scaling and uniform-translation-velocity invariance.

The first absolute check fails because the new oracle assumes 9.81 m/s² gravity.
The frozen shader fixture's `ModelBuilder` instead uses `molla_math::GRAVITY`,
**9.80665 m/s²**, verified in both archived and current sources. This differs from
the actual soil-tractor scene's explicitly configured gravity. Correcting that
input, without changing solver code or tolerance, yields a maximum normalized
full-force residual of **2.2621186966818725e-7** and dt-scaled rate error of
**6.249486873831054e-8** across all ten records. The 1e-6/1e-5 gates pass.
The initial failure is preserved; geometry/rate guards and a builder-gravity
regression now prevent silent fixture reinterpretation.

This is full-force balance under the existing load sequence, not a replacement
for the incremental test: the latter still fails after gravity/bias cancellation
and normalization against the much smaller changed load. Both results must be
retained. Full inverse-operator coverage, ideal-pose accuracy, ordinary compiled
reference parity, integrated trajectory and runtime admission remain open.
No GPU was launched and production acceleration remains unchanged.
[Absolute-balance code, failures and verification](benchmarks/soil/2026-10-12-acceleration-balance/SUMMARY.md).

The parallel CPU reopen failures led to a deterministic duplicate-descriptor

releases it; dropping an observation/task handle still cannot unlock an active
worker. Closing an old duplicate cannot unlock a later independent owner.

passes **29**, including asynchronous lock retention and four real subprocess

confirms the descriptor lifetime behavior. A historical fork/exec interleaving
was not traced; the reproduced ownership defect and repaired parallel lane are

The formulation follows the complementarity identity documented in the

but its status alone never authorizes publication.

Standalone publication owns 327,984 bytes at C=4096,n=32. Hot calls retain one

## Single-dispatch nonlinear prototype — 2026-10-10

Implemented an experimental resident nonlinear driver with paired accepted and
trial impulses, at most 64 Newton steps, 64 inner iterations, 16 backtracking
trials and eight damped-LSQR attempts. It reuses the operator/Krylov formulas,
owns 19,546,208 bytes for 4096 slots/K=64 and exposes impulses only. There is
no host readback or buffer allocation inside the solve; hot counters assert
one dispatch, zero allocations and zero upload/readback traffic.

Three two-contact scenes, the seven-contact scene and 65 contacts pass
independent physical checks. The latter takes five Newton steps, 54 linear
iterations and six trial evaluations, with independent physical error 7.99e-9.
Sparse 65-of-4096 state reuse, poisoned scratch, warm start, upstream/input
faults, explicit reset and one-step bounded rejection pass in `reuse.log`.

This is **not an accepted nonlinear solver**. The 32-DOF case stalls and reaches
64 steps at physical error 1.555e-4. Requiring certified GMRES directions avoids
accepting failed inner solves but does not resolve that trajectory. An
actual/predicted-decrease damping variant regresses the seven-contact fixture,
hits the unchanged readback deadline and is reverted. The saved wide state
after four steps reproduces standalone GPU linear failure (1.2394652e-5 relative
residual at 64 iterations); local operator comparisons pass. The f64 reference
takes 58 further steps from that state, versus four from zero, so the issue
cannot be attributed solely to resident GPU execution.

The actual normal/old-friction/new-friction snapshots reject with line-search

## Workgroup-resident linear directions — 2026-10-10

Added bounded flexible GMRES with local block inverses and an independent
undamped LSQR entry point. Both execute inner iterations on device, using two
dispatches per solve and retained storage. Neither automatically retries the
other or changes the 64-iteration limit. Success requires recomputing Jd+F;
the recurrence estimate alone cannot clear the fault. The test linear bound
is 1e-5; the separate physical publication certificate remains 1e-6.

Owned storage is `(308 + 64 * iterations) * max(contacts,1) + 48` bytes, or
18,038,832 bytes at 4096 slots and 64 iterations. Input/device/budget checks
precede allocation. Hot encoding checks observe no GPU buffer allocations or
host transfers. This is resource evidence, not a throughput benchmark.

The initial resident forward product was wrong on contact 65, when a lane
processed its second contact. Explicitly zeroing each contact's point
accumulator repairs the discrepancy. The regression compares resident and
standalone forward/transpose products at 7, 64, 65 and 129 contacts. After the
repair, GMRES solves the 65-contact case in six iterations at true relative
residual 4.285795e-7; LSQR takes 43 iterations at 9.910913e-6. Earlier failed
variants and their logs are retained rather than attributed to conditioning.

The final combined operator/Krylov suite passes all 11 tests in 44.00 seconds,
including sparse poison/reuse, sticky fault/reset and bounded rejection for
both methods. Format and whitespace checks pass. These are component-test
durations, not frame-performance measurements.

All three saved actual-input initial linear systems pass GPU and independent
f64 residual checks: 195/203/203 active contacts, three GMRES iterations each,
relative residuals 2.8279158e-6, 3.4116993e-6 and 3.366632e-6. This does not
solve the nonlinear captured problems, publish physical outputs or establish
tractor performance. The tests still reconstruct response columns from f64
mass inverses rounded to f32, not the runtime preparation kernel.

Next: nonlinear state updates and globalization, regularized directions,
physical publication and actual runtime integration. No production selection,
physical threshold, full-workload deadline or acceptance target changed.

[Implementation, preserved failures and verification](benchmarks/soil/2026-10-10-newton-resident-krylov/SUMMARY.md).

Implemented an explicit compact GPU observation for unilateral coupling: each body reports positively loaded node count, total normal impulse, impulse-weighted corrected soil velocity and tangential machine-point-minus-soil velocity in world m/s. Machine point motion includes angular velocity and moment arms at the same contact configuration. No support reports `None` rather than zero slip. This is not a normalized wheel-slip ratio or a new friction law; the existing nominal stationary-ground ratio remains separately labelled.

`RigidWorld::read_mpm_soil_contact_motion` and the tractor wrapper return only committed-frame data with stable body identities. Both prepared parities retain **96 bytes/body + 16 bytes** each; five bodies add **992 bytes** total. There is no added stepping dispatch/readback. Explicit observation runs one workgroup per body and downloads **240 bytes** for the tractor. `SOIL_TRACTOR_BENCH_CONTACT_MOTION=1` enables `contact-motion.jsonl` in unilateral benchmarks, with separate observation wall time and traffic outside physics timing.

The rotated/moving-soil/65-slot GPU fixture passes. The actual six-body/65-particle runtime test passes in **248.05 seconds**, including cold construction: three-substep parity alternation, frame/duration/body identity, nonzero tine support, unloaded-wheel `None`, exact compact traffic, zero observation buffer allocation, rollback rejection/resume and empty-soil rejection. Ten benchmark/configuration tests plus retained-capacity checks pass. This is actual tine contact evidence, not yet loaded-wheel or 50k logging acceptance. Stale model edits are rejected in code but need a dedicated runtime check. Real-time, friction, calibration and the complete S08 gate remain open. [Implementation and bounded evidence](benchmarks/soil/2026-10-10-contact-motion/SUMMARY.md).

## Ordered normal-contact cache experiment — 2026-10-10

The actual saved tractor inputs contain 203/240 occupied contacts in 777/921-slot prefixes. Implemented bounded ascending caches with complete original-scan fallback above 256 contacts. Both serial and parallel construction preserve bitwise outputs and the independent f64 oracle, but performance does not justify promotion: the serial later-input sample regresses **1.665792 → 1.812832 ms**; parallel samples give **1.857440 → 1.849312 ms** with large slow outliers, and **1.054496 → 1.066560 ms** on the earlier input. **Production is unchanged.**

The parallel candidate remains test-only, with 1,296 bytes of additional workgroup storage and no additional device buffers/dispatches. A new regression covers sparse/empty/256-boundary/overflow, hard rows, changing occupancy, inactive invalid input and recovery. Six normal GPU suites, five floor suites and two CPU checks pass. Paired replay now accepts a candidate shader path without production edits. No full benchmark was run; do not repeat these rejected candidates unchanged. [Implementation and bounded evidence](benchmarks/soil/2026-10-10-normal-contact-cache/SUMMARY.md).

## XYZ-only position product experiment — 2026-10-10

A test-only variant omits the discarded scalar output of the final compensated quaternion multiplication in position rotation, preserving XYZ arithmetic. **13,017 helper cases** under two rounding modes and translated corrected-drift/dynamics comparisons have zero mismatched physical state/residue words. However, seven paired GPU steps total **25.293920 → 25.208992 ms** for ordinary dynamics (only 0.34% lower, with some steps slower), and **17.365376 → 16.881184 ms** for drift. This does not establish a robust speedup, so **production promotion was rejected**. The production shader is restored byte-for-byte; the candidate survives only under test configuration. No full benchmark was run and no acceptance gate changed. [Experiment and source identity](benchmarks/soil/2026-10-10-position-product/SUMMARY.md).

The zero-position shortcut now also passes focused corrected-drift and mutable-constraint comparisons against test-only programs with only that guard removed. Both retain storage coordinate rounding. [Coverage and bounded commands](benchmarks/soil/2026-10-10-zero-rotation-coverage/SUMMARY.md).

## Exact-zero machine position rotation — 2026-10-09

The ordinary compensated machine shader now skips two quaternion multiplications when the position high/low pair is exactly zero and every quaternion component is finite. Bitwise magnitude checks preserve tiny nonzero/subnormal offsets; all other inputs retain the original arithmetic. **4,824 GPU component cases** pass under storage/shared rounding, including signed zeros and nonfinite fallback. Three six-body tractors at origins 0/1024/65536 remain bit-identical through refresh and seven dynamics steps; paired GPU totals fall **105.427040 → 64.761504 ms**. Seven CPU tests and the facade release build pass.

The changed native 50k unilateral workload completes 33 frames with zero hot GPU buffer allocations. Wall median is **220.259558 ms** (previous sequential run 310.841679 ms), p95 **238.862642 ms**. Machine dynamics falls to **108.018496 ms**, corrected drift **27.910528 ms**; contact projection is **65.613824 ms**. These sequential full-run observations are not alternating-pair acceptance, and all measured frames still miss 60 Hz. Independent velocity differences reach **5.3405762e-5**, above the unchanged 2e-5 gate; other machine fields and final particle positions remain within that bound. Actual coupled corrected-drift equivalence, constrained-model coverage and the full acceptance scope remain open. [Implementation, paired component evidence, full timings and preserved failures](benchmarks/soil/2026-10-09-zero-position-rotation/SUMMARY.md).

## Deferred final momentum check — 2026-10-09

The experimental unilateral normal solver now evaluates its compensated published-momentum residual only after the original direction, impulse and internal residual convergence conditions hold. Nonconverged Newton iterations skip that unused calculation; final acceptance, hard-row handling and numerical bounds are unchanged. Scratch grows by 16 aligned bytes; no GPU buffer or dispatch is added. Ten normal/floor GPU suites and two CPU tests pass. Both actual saved cases remain bit-identical across eight paired trials with their f64 oracle gates; GPU lower medians improve **1.161856 → 1.050336 ms** and **1.901664 → 1.668960 ms**. All **1,122** live normal solves also match the archived shader bit-for-bit.

The separate changed 50k workload completes 33 frames: wall median **310.841679 ms**, p95 **329.691379 ms**, contact-projection median **65.607680 ms**, zero hot GPU buffer allocations. Every measured frame still misses 60 Hz. The previous full-run wall/contact medians were 324.198409 / 72.313856 ms; these are sequential observations, not a paired whole-frame speedup proof. Independent trajectories still exceed 2e-5 for six joint-rate/body-angular-velocity values (maximum **2.6702881e-5**); final particle differences remain below the bound. No accuracy gate was loosened or full-plan acceptance claimed. [Implementation, exact comparisons, full timings and remaining failure](benchmarks/soil/2026-10-09-lazy-publication/SUMMARY.md).

## Shared rounding on identical coupled dynamics/drift inputs — 2026-10-09

Extended the existing test-only live probe to shared rounding and the post-soil corrected drift, preserving projected rates and compensated input state. A first diagnostic failed because it attempted a transfer copy into the storage-only velocity-delta destination; its output is not valid rounding-parity evidence. A retained u32 compute copy repairs the diagnostic without widening production usage flags, and its 65-word regression passes in **0.18 seconds**.

The corrected actual native 50k unilateral tractor run passes in **420.97 seconds** including cold construction: **33 committed frames**, **1,122 dynamics + 1,122 corrected-drift comparisons**, **460,020 physical/status words**, **zero mismatches**. Independent JSONL coverage verifies both complete sequences and source hashes match. This supports sampled same-input equivalence, not independent-trajectory repeatability, production timing, long-horizon acceptance or the 4 ms target. Shared rounding remains experimental, and all prior gates remain unchanged. [Failure, repair, exact coverage and reproduction](benchmarks/soil/2026-10-09-live-rounding-drift/SUMMARY.md).

## Native parallel-stencil experiment — 2026-10-09

A test-only split transfer computes each particle's existing stress once, then distributes its 27 native-atomic deposits across multiple threads. Both 32-thread and four-thread variants pass zero/one/65-particle boundary checks and eight same-input pairs on the saved evolved 50k state, with the original absolute 2e-5 field bound, identical positive-mass support and unchanged particle/history bytes. Both are slower than ordinary native scatter: transfer GPU medians **0.074256 → 0.128048 ms** (32 threads), and **0.074192 → 0.108672 ms** (four threads). Each requires a 2.4 MB cache. Both are rejected for production promotion; no default or numerical threshold changed. Each evolved comparison completes in **0.63 seconds**, avoiding another cold tractor run. These transfer timings do not include complete simulation, contact or rendering. The full target remains unmet. [Implementation, failed performance hypotheses and bounded evidence](benchmarks/soil/2026-10-09-native-stencil/SUMMARY.md).

Added a test-only evolved-state capture after 15 committed frames of the actual native 50k tractor, followed by six reset/P2G/grid-update evaluations without advancing particles. Uniform capture uses a legal GPU uniform-to-storage copy rather than widening production buffer usage. The small capture/restore fixture passes; actual capture completes in **190.37 seconds** including construction, and standalone replay in **0.55 seconds**.

This identifies a varying upstream stage, not the full cause or amplification of the independent-trajectory differences. All particle/history checkpoint bytes remain unchanged. ## Publication optimization and runtime differential check — 2026-10-09

Published momentum validation now computes independent per-DOF finite-contact sums cooperatively, while retaining the original compensated arithmetic order, hard multiplier accumulation and acceptance bound. Scratch grows by 16 bytes per DOF; no production buffer or dispatch is added. Both saved cases remain bit-identical against the preceding repaired shader: **1.672832 → 1.157504 ms** and **2.399040 → 1.906816 ms** in alternating paired GPU measurements. Ten normal/floor GPU suites and two CPU tests pass. A lower-triangle/separate-warp variant was slower and reverted.

The actual 50k run completes 33 frames with zero hot GPU buffer allocations. Median wall is **324.198409 ms**, contact projection **72.313856 ms**, dynamics **182.824640 ms**; all 30 measured 60 Hz deadlines are missed. Independent trajectories differ beyond 2e-5 (maximum generalized-rate difference 0.00231156; particle-coordinate difference 0.002286762 m), so this is not integrated parity or performance acceptance.

A new test-only GPU shadow comparator evaluates the previous and optimized normal shaders on every identical resident input during a full tractor diagnostic. **All 1,122 solves across both state parities match every status/rate/impulse/velocity word**, in a 205.18-second test including cold construction. A helper deliberately corrupts a reference output and verifies detection without changing candidate results. No shadow resource exists in ordinary builds. This supports the optimization on sampled runtime inputs, but does not establish whole-trajectory repeatability or prove the cause of the independent-run divergence. Keep that accuracy issue, the 4 ms target, rendering/export, long-horizon behavior and calibration open. [Evidence and failed comparison](benchmarks/soil/2026-10-09-normal-publication/SUMMARY.md).

## Normal-solver parallelization — 2026-10-09

The optional unilateral solver now distributes contact validation/evaluation and independent matrix rows across GPU lanes, bounds repeated scans to the validated contributing prefix, and publishes soil velocities in its existing parallel recovery pass. All padding still receives validation/reset; a new retained regression covers shrinking extents and invalid trailing data. Device-buffer allocation and dispatch counts are unchanged; conservative workgroup scratch increases by 16 bytes.

Compensated gradient sums fix the second saved tractor failure: the old internal residual understated the f64 published momentum residual (1.51855 times its limit at DOF 3). The repaired case converges in three iterations, with independent rate/impulse errors below 1e-6 and a published residual ratio of 0.328435. No bound was loosened. Both captures pass, as do ten normal/floor GPU suites and two CPU tests.

The earlier successful saved case measures **42.682048 ms serial versus 1.553568 ms candidate**, using alternating same-input GPU timestamps and independent f64 checks. The later baseline fails, so its 836.408992 ms versus 2.235488 ms repaired result is not an equal-work throughput claim. The changed-source actual 50k workload now completes **33 frames / 0.55 simulated seconds**, with workload/source exits 0 and zero hot GPU buffer allocations. Thirty measured frames have median wall **342.779768 ms**, contact projection **89.518080 ms**, machine dynamics **184.321568 ms** and corrected drift **46.217856 ms**. Every measured frame still misses 60 Hz; renderer/export are excluded. No 4 ms/60 FPS, long-horizon or calibrated-soil acceptance is established.
