## Instructions

- Implementation first, followed by focused checks; no repeated broad test suites.
- Use Make/Nix and the live driver; patch tools for editing, no Python edits.
- Preserve source/physical behavior, no unrelated application shutdowns or source edits, no commits/pushes.
- Full physical integration and absolute runtime gates remain required. A component speedup is not application acceptance.
- The user confirmed the RTX 4080 / one tractor and implement / 50k active particles / 60 FPS / soil ≤4 ms per 1/60 simulated second target. No measured soil/traction dataset is available; numerical verification does not establish physical calibration.

## Discoveries

- `MpmSimulation` does not consume `host_pos`/`host_vel` in GPU stepping; scene 122's particle mirror was serving CPU terrain reconstruction and statistics, not an additional required physical solver input. Its physical consumers can use the existing raster maps, while optional particle statistics reduce on-device.
- WGSL reserves `active`; the initial summary shader failed parsing and was corrected to `active_count`. The repaired real-adapter bridge tests pass.
- A newly written paired-MPM test initially required bitwise equality of independent GPU histories. The plan explicitly does not require that for unordered reductions; the test now uses the existing 2e-5 trajectory tolerance and logs errors. The focused run measured maximum position error 7.45e-9 and velocity error 2.86e-6. No existing numerical gate was relaxed.
- Material buffers can be shared between unchanged Bekker terrain snapshots, but overwriting them in place on an edit would mutate older returned views or a cloned owner's state. Edits now replace only the changed map buffer. A retained kernel lifetime token, not native numeric device IDs, identifies the producing cache context; correctly paired device/queue/kernel arguments remain a caller requirement.
- Scene 122's compaction/rut summary scans are observation-only, but its full terrain/particle snapshots still feed physical queries and rendering. Disabling summary scans must not remove those snapshots before their consumers migrate.
- Live GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4080, Vulkan, driver 595.91.07. Commands use `NVIDIA_VERSION=595.91.07 nix develop --impure -c make ...` because `nixVulkan` is provided by the dev shell, not the initial host PATH.
- MPM export can preserve border clamping, compaction maxima and velocity averages with histogram → hierarchical exclusive scan → scatter → per-cell workgroup reduction. It no longer needs one complete particle scan per terrain cell.
- A 64-lane workgroup reduces each occupied cell, including cells with more than 65,536 particles; there is no fixed bucket capacity that silently drops members. Hierarchical scans and two-dimensional dispatch cover grids beyond one dispatch dimension.
- Reusing immutable prepared bindings avoids substep parameter overwrite hazards. The simulation cache keys particle count, actual raster parameters/fallback velocity, and output buffer identities; changing any of these prepares a new export. Fixed matching parameters reuse the same resources.
- Empty MPM terrain export now writes the declared rest height/fallback velocity rather than leaving old output untouched.
- DEM bins are only a candidate index. Final membership retains the original half-open world-coordinate predicate; external grains are excluded from physical cells even though their lookup bins are clamped. Each output cell searches the bin range covered by its rounded endpoints before reducing height and top-layer velocity.
- Decimal boundaries exposed fused versus separate multiply/add rounding. The new DEM bounds use explicit WGSL `fma`; the CPU oracle uses `mul_add`, matching the unchanged legacy raster on this NVIDIA/Vulkan adapter. Test fixtures normalize subnormal coordinates to zero. WGSL permits different rounding and subnormal handling, so this is not a cross-adapter bitwise guarantee; other adapters must rerun parity rather than silently relax count checks. See [WGSL floating-point evaluation](https://www.w3.org/TR/WGSL/#floating-point-evaluation).
- Viewer source was not fully rustfmt-normalized at the start. Unrelated formatting changes were removed; only the intended selection/test edits remain in that file.
- Engram tools were discovered as unavailable. This report records the checkpoint without claiming an external memory save.
- A new symmetric, high-speed collision fixture exposed cumulative CPU/GPU trajectory drift already shared by full rebuild and refit: at step 7 both differ from independent CPU evolution by 0.0001783371 m/s, while rebuild/refit differ by only 0.00000040233135 m/s. The refit gate therefore separately checks exact GPU contact sets against exhaustive CPU enumeration, each force/integration step against a same-input CPU oracle, and the full trajectory against full GPU rebuild at the unchanged 2e-5 tolerance. Independent CPU trajectory error is retained as diagnostic evidence, not mislabeled as refit error or silently erased.
- Cross-instance wgpu device/queue equality is insufficient: native equality compares numeric object IDs, which can collide across independently created instances. A wrong-device regression reached an invalid buffer lookup before this was discovered. The resident owner now checks retained native HAL device/queue identities before writes; this supports the configured native Vulkan/Metal/DX12 paths and rejects unsupported identity backends explicitly. The four focused resident tests now pass on Vulkan; other backends remain unverified. Initial construction still requires a correctly paired device/queue from the caller.

## Accomplished

### MPM particle-binned export

- Added `PreparedTireMpmRaster`, with caller-encoder recording and no allocation, submission or readback inside `encode`.
- Added parallel histogram/scatter, hierarchical prefix scan and per-cell reduction shaders. Total work is proportional to particles plus raster cells (fixed workgroup-size scan/reduction factors), rather than cells multiplied by all particles.
- The existing `dispatch_raster_to_buffers` API uses the optimized path. Explicit exhaustive reference dispatch remains available. A prepared exhaustive reference permits matched-buffer comparisons without charging allocations to only one side.
- `MpmSimulation::raster_tire_fem_terrain_gpu_resident_with` caches the prepared export. Existing callers, including scene 122, therefore use the optimized export without creating scratch/bind groups every call when parameters and buffer identities remain unchanged.
- Added checked dimension multiplication, storage size/usage/device-capacity checks and finite fallback-velocity validation for preparation. This does not establish all broader public API/device-loss guarantees in the full plan.

### Production selection

- Scene 122 defaults to MPM only, not simultaneous MPM and Bekker updates.
- Production UI selects MPM/Bekker/DEM/no soil exclusively. Explicit comparison mode retains independent toggles and documents which selected terrain supplies FEM contact.
- Leaving comparison mode retains the previous MPM → Bekker → DEM contact priority and enables only that backend.

### Dirty material maps and optional soil summaries

- Added uniform friction/film setters to `TireBekkerFemTerrainOwner`. Unchanged uniform values take a constant-time path without allocating or refilling a host map. Generic map setters compare values and invalidate only the changed GPU map. Invalid dimensions or nonfinite uniform values return an error without modifying the previous map.
- Resident terrain views reuse unchanged friction, film and surface-velocity buffers. Changed maps allocate a replacement instead of rewriting a buffer held by an earlier view; cloned owners remain independent. Replacement kernels, including kernels on another device, invalidate all cached map buffers.
- Scene 122 uses the uniform setters and reports setter errors. Removed a discarded `fem_contact_terrain()` clone from the Bekker summary path.
- Added an opt-in MPM/Bekker summary checkbox, off by default. The shared single-pass summary function returns before visiting data when disabled. Physics snapshots are unchanged; UI labels retained numbers as last samples. DEM mirrored reports, rendering and other physical/diagnostic consumers are still part of the remaining residency work.
- The final two focused GPU cache tests passed. With three 9-cell maps, first population adds exactly 3 explicit buffer allocations / 216 uploaded bytes; unchanged maps add 0 / 0; editing one scalar map adds 1 / 36. These are measured deltas excluding the unchanged Bekker solver's own allocations/transfers, not a whole-step zero-allocation claim or latency benchmark. Final verification after the uniform-equality refinement and viewer changes passed all nine selected checks (six CPU/contract, three GPU); the command chain exited 0.

### MPM terrain-only physical bridge and compact diagnostics

- Added `PreparedTireMpmTerrainReadback` with retained staging/source handles/device/queue. `read_blocking` copies existing height/sinkage/surface-velocity buffers in one submission/map/wait; preparation validates dimensions, byte capacities, usages and summary dispatch limits. Correctly paired source buffers/device/queue remain the preparation caller's responsibility.
- An optional 64-lane workgroup reduction computes compaction maximum and active-particle count. It adds 16 bytes to the same mapped range, with no particle transfer and no extra wait. Disabled diagnostics encode no summary dispatch and omit those bytes. Repeated reads allocate no explicit GPU buffers or uniforms.
- `MpmSimulation::prepare_tire_terrain_readback_with` binds the current live compaction buffer/count. Callers reprepare after source/count/dimension changes. This is a blocking physical bridge, not a revisioned asynchronous telemetry ring.
- Scene 122 no longer calls `tire_fem_terrain_owner_with`. It retains one terrain snapshot for CPU carcass/contact queries and forwards existing GPU maps to GPU FEM feedback. Its optional summary uses compact GPU results. Reset/size changes invalidate the prepared bridge; step/raster/readback errors are surfaced instead of ignored. UI explicitly labels the blocking terrain-only bridge. The explicitly selected CPU feedback/reference mode still downloads particles for CPU feedback.
- Two kernel GPU tests pass. The paired solver test passes six feedback/MPM windows with alternating diagnostics, unchanged height/sinkage maps, surface-velocity tolerance 2e-5, final trajectory tolerance 2e-5, and empty reset. Measured logical download: 12,336 bytes for 257-particle full-state export versus 840 bytes for 35 terrain cells, or 856 with statistics. No steady-state bridge buffer allocation/upload was recorded; this excludes the solver/feedback's own allocations and backend staging behavior.
- `make check APP_TARGET='-p molla_viewer'` passed. The short release bridge benchmark passed after a first adapter-unavailable attempt under heavy external load. Final `make test-soil-gpu PHASE=S03` passed all seven selected GPU tests, and the three viewer soil contracts passed. All owned processes are terminal; no end-to-end speedup or S03 completion is claimed.

### DEM export and shared bin infrastructure

- Shared `soil_particle_raster.rs` and `soil_raster_bins.wgsl` own histogram, hierarchical prefix scan, scatter, scratch validation and ordered encode dispatch. MPM and DEM retain separate material/membership reductions.
- `dispatch_resident_terrain_raster` now selects binned GPU export. The previous shader and dispatch remain available through `dispatch_resident_terrain_raster_reference`; no CPU fallback was introduced.
- Public `PreparedTireDemRaster` and `prepare_resident_terrain_raster` bind persistent reference/output/state buffers. Ordered encodes allocate and download nothing. The convenience dispatch still allocates per call; the live owner now retains its resources as described below.
- DEM preserves floor/reference heights, radius/spacing lower bounds, empty-cell output, the top-surface sentinel, surface-band threshold inclusion and contributing-grain counts. Raster-only empty state is supported; general DEM state creation still requires grains.
- Tests compare CPU half-open oracles, the unchanged exhaustive GPU shader and binned output. They include decimal and exact boundaries, large origins with coarsely represented spacing, multi-level scans, 65,537 crowded grains, 66,049 output cells, changing resident inputs/reference heights, repeated encode, empty/reset behavior and invalid sizes/counts/parameters. Integer contributor counts remain exact; height/sinkage tolerance is 1e-6 and velocity tolerance is 2e-5.

### Focused Make entry points

- `make test-soil-fast PHASE=S02`: CPU dimension/parameter contract test.
- `make test-soil-gpu PHASE=S02`: five hardware raster tests, excluding both performance tests.
- `make test-soil-gpu PHASE=S03`: four resident GPU tests with the new opt-in `resource-counters` feature; benchmark excluded.
- `make bench-soil CASE=raster MODE=compare`: prebuilds release tests, then runs a 30-second-bounded paired export benchmark with source hashes, adapter/hardware metadata, raw timings, summary and exit file.
- `make bench-soil CASE=dem MODE=compare`: matched 50k-particle solver+export trajectories, four physical substeps per sample, twelve alternating paired samples and final state/terrain parity; 30-second execution deadline after compilation.
- Unimplemented phase/case/mode selections fail explicitly. `PHASE=all`, integrated machine cases and `check-soil-results` are not implemented yet; do not interpret these initial targets as S00/S10 completion.

### Retained DEM step and frame bridge

- `soil_dem_resident.rs` retains two particle states, Morton keys, sorted indices, tree rows, radix scratch, contacts, parameter buffers, bind groups and two prepared terrain exporters. Each substep records Morton generation → stable radix → leaf/internal rebuild → DEM/contact step → terrain export into one encoder/submission. No physical timestep, contact law or candidate cutoff was relaxed.
- Every tree level has its own immutable build uniform. Per-step contacts/parameters are uploaded immediately before their ordered submission; changing-parameter parity covers twelve steps without intervening state downloads. This is not yet a public arbitrary multi-step caller-encoder API.
- `step_sparse_lbvh_gpu_resident` leaves the CPU mirror unchanged, exposes `state_revision`/`mirror_revision`, and provides explicit `refresh_mirror`. Existing `step_sparse_lbvh_gpu_mirrored` remains a synchronous compatibility API using the retained implementation. Reset/capacity changes invalidate or recreate the appropriate owner resources.
- `step_sparse_lbvh_gpu_mirrored_n` advances fixed contacts/parameters for N substeps before one telemetry/state readback. Scene 119 uses it for the existing 16-step, 0.008-second update. The previous code held roller contact inputs constant over those same 16 steps; batching did not freeze a previously reevaluated physical input.
- Viewer particles, roller surface queries and rut measurements still consume a blocking frame snapshot. The UI labels this mode explicitly. Displacement telemetry now spans the last call (the frame in GPU mode), not one substep; the label was updated accordingly. No rendered/integrated visual acceptance is claimed.
- Runtime evidence over eight warmed substeps: zero explicit buffer-allocation observations, zero logical readback bytes, 1152 uploaded bytes, 208 dispatches, stable tree/terrain/ping-pong handles and unchanged live bind-group/pipeline counts. Backend-internal command/staging allocations are outside this observation contract.
- Equivalent 16-step controls read 131584 bytes with per-step snapshots versus 8224 bytes with one frame snapshot, exactly 16× less. Final positions/velocities match within the unchanged 2e-5 tolerance.
- Remaining S03 work includes device-side physical queries, direct/bounded renderer consumption, MPM owner-snapshot removal, asynchronous revisioned telemetry/rings, device loss, and the fully resident application gate. S04's production default still rebuilds the tree every step; optional refit has small-scene checks but fails large-scene trajectory parity, as recorded below.

## Compact-grid verification checkpoint — 2026-10-08

### Goal

Replace full-domain physical MPM grid allocation with checked active-tile storage while preserving dense controls and the full soil-plan scope.

### Instructions

Keep GPU-first ownership, unchanged physical parameters and tolerances, Make-based bounded checks and no unrelated application shutdowns. No commit/push or production-default change.

### Discoveries

- Compact addressing must cover P2G, G2P, rigid/grid sweeps and implicit neighbors. Clearing a retired physical slot must not depend on a page entry that another lane can concurrently invalidate.
- Overflow can occur after some substeps have completed. A fault-aware caller must account for the completed portion and advance only the remainder after growing the pool; reporting an entire batch as advanced would lose physical time.
- World page-table storage still grows with domain extent. Physical-field savings do not establish bounded total field memory or a solver-time improvement.

### Accomplished

- Added `MpmSimulation::new_sparse` with checked fixed tile capacity and dense-backed active mode retained separately. Compact grid arrays allocate 64 physical cell slots per tile. World coordinates remain unsigned through linear indexing; grid/boundary arithmetic uses decoded coordinates.
- Tile marking claims empty page entries with compare-exchange, then publishes a slot. Reset retires the previous slots and page entries before the next build; implicit neighbors outside the map read as inactive rather than aliasing another slot.
- Added a sticky overflow guard and explicit status/error APIs. Particle transfer/plasticity skip work after overflow. Completed substeps are tracked as a wrapping u32 count within a grid epoch, not an all-or-nothing batch result. Explicit reset clears the fault; growth starts a new epoch.
- Added `reserve_sparse_tiles` using the owned device. Growth retains particle, affine, deformation, plastic/compaction and material buffers and replaces only grid resources/bindings outside the hot loop. Shrink requests are no-ops; invalid reservations fail without replacing current storage.
- Final `make test-soil-gpu PHASE=S05` exited 0: four scheduling tests passed in 10.00 seconds and five compact tests passed in 10.96 seconds. - On the tested 64³ fixture, actual grid-buffer sizes sum to 14,712,848 bytes dense versus 246,032 compact. With 64 physical tiles, 32³/96³/512³ domains use 231,696 / 284,944 / 8,618,256 bytes and each schedules eight active tiles for the fixed 129-particle patch. ## Bounded tile-lookup checkpoint — 2026-10-08

### Goal

Remove domain-sized MPM lookup allocation while keeping the full soil implementation goal active.

### Instructions

Keep the dense control, unchanged numerical gates, explicit overflow behavior and implementation-first Make workflow.

### Discoveries

- Retiring a linear-probed hash table cannot search through concurrently erased chains. Each physical tile now retains its insertion bucket, and reset erases exactly that bucket without another lookup.
- World-tile keys publish before slot values within marking, but lookup consumers execute only after the marking pass completes. Duplicate producers do not read unpublished slot values.

### Accomplished

- Compact mode now allocates a power-of-two open-addressed table with at least twice the physical tile capacity. Keys, slot values, tile identities and reverse bucket indices share the existing packed stiffness allocation.
- Grid sweeps address their physical dispatch slot directly; P2G/G2P and implicit neighbors use bounded hash lookup. Dense-backed active mode retains its direct map.
- The nine existing focused checks pass after the change. At fixed 64-tile capacity, 32³/96³/512³/1536³ domains all allocate exactly 230,928 grid/lookup bytes. A remote patch in the 1536³ domain exercises world indices beyond signed-i32 range.

### Next Steps

Verify adversarial collisions and retirement, then add compact storage to the matched benchmark. Persistent field history, large-case torque and performance acceptance remain open.

## Bounded selected disk reads — 2026-10-09

`MpmSoilStore::read_tiles` checks unique-tile, particle and conservative encoded-byte limits before reading selected blobs. Read provenance checks the open handle and committed generation: unchanged saves retain validity, changed generations or reopened handles reject old provenance. Historical selections remain accessible.

Partial reads return a selection rather than a replacement archive. Corruption in an unselected blob is intentionally outside their integrity scope; full load still verifies every referenced blob and global ID. Empty selections read no payload bytes, and read failures neither poison the handle nor publish save-reuse epochs.

## Background selected disk reads — 2026-10-09

`MpmSoilStore::begin_read` moves the exclusive handle into a single worker. Manifest-only preparation validates/deduplicates the request before spawning; owned key storage is bounded by the selected-tile limit. One request and one result slot prevent an unbounded work queue. Payload I/O and decoding run on the worker, not through a synchronous fallback. Thread creation and manifest preparation are still caller work, not hard real-time operations.

`MpmSoilStoreReadTask::poll` reports pending without waiting for filesystem completion, then transfers the store and result once. Preparation/spawn/read errors return the same owner. An unwinding read panic returns a poisoned owner that requires reopen; process-aborting failures are not recoverable. Dropping a pending task does not join, cancel a filesystem call or release the worker's lock early. The lock is released when an abandoned worker finishes and drops its undeliverable result. No duration bound is inferred from byte limits.

Caller lifecycle:

1. Move the store into `begin_read(&wanted_tiles, read_limits)` and retain the returned task between scheduler ticks.
2. Poll once per opportunity, not in a busy-wait loop. `Ok(None)` means pending; an outer error means the task is terminal, not a completed read.
3. On completion, retain `completion.store` before handling `completion.result`, so an ordinary read error does not accidentally drop ownership. A successful inner `None` means no committed manifest; `Some(read)` is a bounded selection, not live GPU state.
4. Call `store.validate_read(&read)` before using its provenance. Preserve the returned store for later work; after a panic-poisoned result, drop/reopen rather than treating the owner as healthy.

The focused release store lane passes **14 tests, 2 ignored**, including deterministic pending/drop lock checks, exact history/provenance preservation, startup failure/early-exit recovery, ordinary I/O recovery, panic poisoning and terminal disconnection. Existing selected-read integrity and subprocess durability checks still pass. The injected panic message in the log is intentional and caught. No GPU workload was rerun for this filesystem-only increment. Full host archive ownership, asynchronous writes, physical sleep/support boundaries and bounded traversal remain open; no S07/full-plan completion or performance gain is claimed. [Commands, results and next steps](benchmarks/soil/2026-10-09-store-background-read/SUMMARY.md).

## Bounded selected durable writeback — 2026-10-09

The store now has a partial-update API distinct from full replacement `save`: `writeback(&read, &updated_checkpoint, limits)`. The read must belong to the same open handle and current generation; updated particle slots follow its sorted global IDs. Shared archive validation rejects count, mass, reference-volume, physical configuration and material-identity changes while allowing evolved positions, velocities and plastic/history state.

Manifest-only preparation bounds the source/destination union before destination payload reads. The retained source snapshot supplies its previously verified records; only previously unselected occupied destinations need loading and merging. Destination hash/metadata/count/coordinate checks and cross-affected ID checks reject invalid merges. Unloaded manifest entries and their blobs are preserved without reading their payloads. Integrity remains scoped to affected data, not a fresh proof of every stored blob. Logical byte limits exclude manifest/container overhead and multiple working copies; manifest cloning/publication still scales with total tile count.

Full and selected saves use the same synced-blob/atomic-HEAD publication implementation. Selected validation or destination-read failure leaves the writer healthy and HEAD unchanged; failures during publication poison the owner and require reopen because a new generation may already be visible. An unchanged or empty selection writes zero bytes and retains the generation. Changed publication invalidates all earlier reads, including those of disjoint tiles.

New stage failures use returned errors, not simulated power loss; no additional GPU or physical traversal acceptance is claimed.

The live `MpmSoilWorld` still owns its full archive. Background selected writeback, disk-backed live transitions, sleep/support physics, field traversal, renderer-inclusive performance and physical calibration remain open. ## Background selected writeback — 2026-10-09

`MpmSoilStore::begin_writeback` now owns one store/read/update request and returns a nonblocking `MpmSoilStoreWritebackTask`. Cheap caller-side checks reject stale/foreign reads and source bounds before spawning. Physical validation, destination loading/merging, blob writes and atomic manifest publication run on the worker. There is no synchronous payload-I/O fallback. This is host persistence work, not a CPU physics path or a hard real-time thread-creation guarantee.

Completion returns the exclusive store, original read, original updated checkpoint and operation result. Startup and ordinary pre-publication validation/read errors preserve retry inputs and a healthy owner. Publication errors or unwinding panics poison the returned owner; drop/reopen and inspect HEAD rather than blindly retrying an old read. The result can be an error even after the new generation was published. Successful changed writes invalidate the returned read's provenance; its historical data remains accessible.

One request/result slot bounds concurrency. Dropping a pending task neither joins nor cancels the write: HEAD may still change, and the worker retains the lock until its work ends. A lost completion does not prove that no write occurred. The caller must retain pending tasks between scheduler ticks, separate completion ownership from result handling, and only advance its durable-state bookkeeping after observing success or resolving HEAD after a failure.

The release store lane passes **27 tests, 2 ignored** in 0.04 seconds after a 14.22-second build. Six new cases verify exact complete archive state, thread/lock ownership, startup failure and retry, valid owner recovery from invalid input, post-publication error and panic recovery, abandoned-task publication, and terminal disconnect behavior. The logged injected panics are expected and caught. Existing selected reads/writes and subprocess durability checks remain green; process abort/power loss is not newly tested. No GPU or full traversal result is inferred from these storage checks. Live disk-backed ownership and all unresolved physical/performance gates remain open. [Evidence](benchmarks/soil/2026-10-09-store-background-write/SUMMARY.md).

## Substep contact-transition isolation — 2026-10-09

Implemented a bounded test-only observer immediately after projected soil response and before compensated machine drift. It reads retained pre-publication inputs and captured outputs/intermediates, plus actual geometry and the correct owner buffer for each resident parity. Every emitted node's reconstructed integer index is checked against exact GPU ownership, and all owned nodes must be represented once. Faults, nonfinite values, ambiguous grid reconstruction and excess records reject. Production builds contain none of the new observer state, accessors or readbacks.

Independent partial/extended 50k trajectories complete 26 frames and each retain **136 substeps across frames 23–26**. The full test passes in **487.82 seconds**, including cold construction, with source/run exits zero. Staging is capped at 4 MiB; JSONL artifacts are about 4.4 MiB each. Two CPU grid-identity/rejection tests and the facade release build pass. Initial compilation missed a direct test fixture's new optional field; that failure and the corrected build are preserved.

The validated trace comparison finds **34 membership disagreements**. First disagreement: committed frame **25**, zero-based substep **15**, tine binding **4**, grid node **122961**. Partial has no boundary node; extended includes **0.47464246 kg** with the +Y normal. Maximum generalized-rate difference increases from **0.00002998114** before projection to **0.00645053387** afterward. Window maximum is **0.01120448112**. Both trajectories already differ before observation begins; all projected rows exceed the strict bound, so this does not identify the earliest varying stage or attribute every discrepancy to membership.

A saved-geometry GPU probe uses the production shader's coordinate, rotation and membership functions. It reproduces the captured exclusion/inclusion in **0.45 seconds**. Signed box margins are **-1.013279 µm partial / +4.559755 µm extended**. This is an actual hard geometric transition, not evidence that the machine scratch arithmetic changed on identical inputs.

A compact exporter preserves active inputs and original slot ordering in the existing binary replay format, zero-filling unused slots and trimming trailing capacity. Both snapshots replay original-order outputs bit-for-bit. Three replay/capture/f64 tests pass in **3.04 seconds**; node permutations remain inside unchanged gates (worst output tolerance ratio **0.09536743**), and frozen-system permutations are exact. For the new occupied snapshot, the independent f64 solution changes by **0.00615081398** when only the normal is disabled and **0.00647188931** when only the node is removed; GPU/oracle errors are at most **1.825e-7**.

This isolates a substantial amplification mechanism in one captured transition. It does not repair physical contact activation, excuse existing trajectory failures or meet performance/calibration gates. No membership predicate, mass threshold, solver tolerance or production default changed. Next work should use these saved inputs with physical gap/withdrawal and conservation contracts, not repeat unchanged cold timing runs. Fully blocked normals still fault pending hard affine row support; runtime defaults, full-workload failures and uncalibrated status are unchanged.

**Subsequent hard-row support:** the wrapper now handles fully blocked normals with exact affine inequalities and a feasible working-set Newton extension. Five floor GPU suites pass in 10.97 seconds, including hard/mixed full-space references, actual negative-multiplier removal, redundant rows, 32 active independent constraints and fail-closed budget/overflow cases. Four term slots per node retain up to three finite hinges plus a terminal hard row. Duplicate hard constraints can have nonunique multiplier distributions; those cases require unique primal agreement and full physical KKT checks, not an arbitrary dual distribution. No actual-tractor speed or trajectory claim follows. [Failures, correction and supported limits](benchmarks/soil/2026-10-09-soil-hard-rows/SUMMARY.md).

Added `soil_normal_projection_gpu` and its facade export, exposing a separately named experimental component rather than silently replacing sticking-volume contact. Each input row represents a distinct scalar soil normal DOF with finite mass `m`, free normal velocity `u`, machine normal Jacobian `a` and nonnegative gap allowance `s = gap / dt`. The condition is `v_soil - a*q + s >= 0`; outward soil impulse is nonnegative and complementary to this slack. Machine reaction is `-a^T*lambda`. Inactive slots have exactly zero mass.

Independent soil velocities can be eliminated, leaving `0.5*(q-q_free)^T*M*(q-q_free) + 0.5*sum(m*max(a*q-u-s,0)^2)`. Recover `lambda=m*max(a*q-u-s,0)` and corrected soil normal velocity. The bounded GPU solve uses semismooth Newton/Cholesky with line search, followed by parallel recovery; encoding makes no submissions, allocations or logical host transfers. Capacity/device/budget checks precede resource creation. Sticky status guards outputs after input, mass, arithmetic, line-search or iteration faults. Callers must check status before publication. The component does not generate contact geometry or advance physical time.

Initial rate-only convergence fails the 1000:1 soil/machine mass ratio's strict impulse gate: **0.99909306 vs 0.999000999**. Added induced-impulse stopping checks. A deliberate active-set crossing then exposes **2.29478e-6** generalized momentum residual against the unchanged **1e-6** scaled gate. Adding residual convergence reveals cancellation in the near-minimum line-search energy difference. Rewriting the same objective difference as gradient slope plus branchwise curvature resolves the cancellation; no oracle threshold or model was loosened. All failed logs/source snapshots are retained.

Final **four GPU suites pass in 3.55 seconds**, and two CPU checks pass. Coverage includes finite mass ratios, gap activation and zero-impulse continuity, separation without attraction, inactive/empty exactness, original-input repeatability, explicit backtracking, **36 seeded exhaustive f64 active-set cases** at widths 1–8 and 32, invalid/asymmetric input, sticky/reset faults, exhausted-iteration refusal and allocation-free rejection paths. An 860 kg six-DOF body with six spatial contact rows passes f64 rates/impulses, complementarity and kinetic-energy checks; maximum linear/angular impulse errors are **4.465e-6 / 2.448e-6**. Hot encode observes zero GPU buffer allocations and zero logical host uploads/readbacks. These are component checks, not whole-simulator latency or calibration evidence.

The contact/free-motion split is informed by [MPM/articulated convex contact](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.13783v2) and [SAP](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.10107); the implemented frictionless independent-normal reduction is not either paper's full method. Shared-grid-DOF coupling, fixed-boundary constraints, friction, gap/penetration geometry, runtime transaction integration and agricultural verification remain open. In particular, duplicating one soil DOF as several independent rows would be an invalid approximation. Existing runtime defaults and the failed full-trajectory gates remain unchanged. [Derivation, source archives and commands](benchmarks/soil/2026-10-09-unilateral-soil-normal/SUMMARY.md).

## Key Learnings

1. MPM export is now a bounded-pass particle-binning pipeline, with a measured component improvement rather than a claimed whole-simulator speedup.
2. Caching must include output buffer identity and particle count to survive resets and replacement correctly.
3. DEM needs rounded half-open membership and a second, surface-band-filtered velocity reduction; sharing bin infrastructure must not merge the two material contracts.
4. Decimal-boundary CPU/GPU comparisons need an explicit arithmetic contract and an actual legacy GPU control, not simply a looser velocity tolerance.
5. Native wgpu numeric IDs can collide across instances; retained HAL object identity detects foreign device/queue use before touching resident buffers.
6. Removing allocation/readback overhead is not enough: the measured 50k DEM solver+export path still runs slower than simulated time.
7. A material cache must preserve previously returned views and cloned owners; replacing only edited buffers keeps snapshot semantics without unchanged-map uploads.
8. Physical terrain queries can consume the already rasterized maps without owning all MPM particles; compact GPU statistics keep optional diagnostics from reintroducing particle downloads.
